papers.title: Focused Omni-Modal GUI Agents
papers.abstract: Abstract FocusGUI is a lightweight adapter that dynamically selects relevant multimodal evidence for GUI agents to prevent compounding errors from irrelevant context, improving action accuracy without fine-tuning the backbone.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Graphical User Interface (GUI) agents increasingly act over streaming omni-modal observations spanning screenshots, audio, video, interaction history, and device states. However, exposing this complete context uniformly at every step ignores that relevance is transient and sparse: the signal determining one action can become clutter at the next. Because executed actions feed back into the context, these errors compound into Sequential Distraction, driving the agent into irreversible trajectory drift. We formulate the underlying requirement as Focused Perception: a representation that is step-adaptive, action-sufficient, and non-intrusive. We realize this in FocusGUI, a lightweight adapter that dynamically prioritizes multimodal channels against a step-specific decision reference. Instead of uniformly processing all inputs, it compresses the most relevant evidence into a compact latent and subtly injects it into the frozen decoder's embeddings, guiding the model's attention without altering its native parameter space. FocusGUI trains from action supervision alone, requiring neither modality-relevance labels nor backbone fine-tuning. Across four omni-modal backbones, it raises overall Type Match by +33.2 and Exact Match by 3.0 times over the frozen backbone on average, and Type Match by +30.1 over the strongest existing enhancement method.

ru.title: Фокус на главном: адаптер, который не даёт GUI-агенту сбиться с пути
ru.desc: В статье рассматриваются GUI-агенты, которые действуют по потоковым мультимодальным данным (скриншоты, аудио, видео, история взаимодействий), и показано, что нерелевантный контекст приводит к каскадным ошибкам, названным «Sequential Distraction». Авторы предлагают принцип Focused Perception и реализуют его в FocusGUI — легковесном адаптере, который динамически выбирает наиболее значимые модальности, сжимает их в компактный латентный вектор и внедряет в эмбеддинги замороженного декодера. Метод обучается только на данных о действиях, без разметки релевантности модальностей и без дообучения backbone. В экспериментах на четырёх omni-modal моделях FocusGUI в среднем повышает Type Match на 33.2 пункта и Exact Match в 3 раза относительно замороженной модели.

en.title: Dynamic Relevance for Accurate GUI Actions
en.desc: FocusGUI is a novel lightweight adapter designed to enhance the performance of GUI agents by dynamically selecting the most relevant multimodal evidence from various inputs like screenshots, audio, and interaction history. This approach addresses the issue of Sequential Distraction, where irrelevant context can lead to compounding errors in decision-making. By implementing Focused Perception, FocusGUI adapts its representation based on the current action, ensuring that only the most pertinent information is processed at each step. Remarkably, it achieves significant improvements in action accuracy without the need for fine-tuning the underlying model or requiring additional labels for modality relevance.

zh.title: 动态聚焦，提升多模态决策准确性
zh.desc: FocusGUI 是一个轻量级适配器，能够动态选择与 GUI 代理相关的多模态证据，从而避免因无关上下文导致的复合错误，提高动作准确性，而无需对基础模型进行微调。随着 GUI 代理在流式多模态观察中执行任务，完整的上下文在每一步都可能变得冗余，因此需要关注瞬时和稀疏的相关性。FocusGUI 通过压缩最相关的证据并将其注入到解码器的嵌入中，指导模型的注意力，而不改变其原有的参数空间。该方法仅依赖于动作监督进行训练，无需模态相关标签或基础模型微调，显著提高了多模态任务的匹配精度。

papers.title: Matrix-Game 4.0: Harnessing Video Models for Real-Time Playable Game Worlds
papers.abstract: Abstract Matrix-Game 4.0 separates game logic from visual synthesis via an executable engine and autoregressive video renderer, achieving real-time interactive gameplay with low latency.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Moving from controllable videos to genuinely playable worlds requires persistent world state, executable game rules, and low-latency interaction. We outline a roadmap for the next generation of Matrix-Game that separates game execution from visual generation through an executable game harness, and introduce Matrix-Game 4.0 as the first system built on this design. A lightweight game engine maintains world state and executes interaction rules, a multimodal coding agent translates player ideas into game code and dynamic scene captions, and a renderer based on autoregressive video model transforms engine-rendered low-poly proxies into detailed visuals, conditioned on dynamic captions and memory references. This framework provides continuous guidance for visual generation and enables natural-language creation and modification of scenes and gameplay. Our renderer is trained on aligned low-poly and high-fidelity video pairs and distilled into a causal generator that generates in four-frame chunks with one or two denoising steps. Together with targeted inference optimizations, Matrix-Game 4.0 enables 480p, 60 FPS gameplay on a single NVIDIA RTX5090 with a key-press-to-display latency of 112ms. Single-step generation achieves 83FPS steady-state throughput with 18.2GiB of peak GPU memory usage. With fixed prompts, steady-state throughput also reaches 67FPS on an RTX5080 and 58FPS on an RTX5070Ti. We demonstrate customizable shooter and driving games with engine-enforced mechanics, and release code, model weights, and low-poly game assets to support research and creation of playable game worlds.

ru.title: Игровой движок отвечает за логику, нейросеть за картинку — играем в мир в реальном времени
ru.desc: Статья представляет Matrix-Game 4.0, систему, которая разделяет игровую логику и визуальную генерацию: лёгкий игровой движок хранит состояние мира и исполняет правила, а мультимодальный coding agent превращает идеи игрока в код и динамические описания сцены. Визуализацию выполняет autoregressive video model, который преобразует низкополигональные прокси в детальное изображение, обусловленное captions и memory references. Рендерер обучен на парах low-poly и high-fidelity видео и дистиллирован в causal generator, генерирующий по четыре кадра за раз с одним или двумя шагами денойзинга. Благодаря оптимизациям инференса система достигает 480p при 60 FPS на одной GPU RTX5090 с задержкой 112 мс.

en.title: Revolutionizing Game Development with Matrix-Game 4.0
en.desc: Matrix-Game 4.0 introduces a new way to create interactive video games by separating the game's logic from its visuals. This system uses a lightweight game engine to manage the game's state and rules, while an autoregressive video renderer generates high-quality graphics in real-time. Players can interact with the game using natural language, allowing them to create and modify scenes easily. The framework achieves low-latency gameplay and high frame rates, making it suitable for immersive gaming experiences.

zh.title: Matrix-Game 4.0：游戏逻辑与视觉合成的完美分离
zh.desc: Matrix-Game 4.0 是一种新型游戏框架，它将游戏逻辑与视觉合成分离，使用可执行引擎和自回归视频渲染器，实现低延迟的实时互动游戏。该系统通过轻量级游戏引擎维护世界状态，并执行互动规则，同时多模态编码代理将玩家的想法转化为游戏代码和动态场景字幕。自回归视频模型的渲染器将低多边形代理转换为详细视觉效果，支持自然语言创建和修改场景及游戏玩法。Matrix-Game 4.0 使得在单个 NVIDIA RTX5090 上以 480p、60 FPS 的速度运行游戏成为可能，且具有较低的按键到显示延迟。

papers.title: Ropedia W0: Scaling Loco-Manipulation World Models across Embodiments with Human Experience
papers.abstract: Abstract Ropedia W0 is a world foundation model for cross-embodiment loco-manipulation that unifies human and robot data via kinematic representations and achieves state-of-the-art results across diverse benchmarks.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small World models enable embodied agents to anticipate action consequences, yet jointly modeling locomotion and manipulation across diverse embodiments remains challenging due to heterogeneous action spaces and limited multimodal supervision. We present Ropedia W0, the first egocentric loco-manipulation world foundation model spanning humans and robots with diverse embodiments. We curate Xp-Data, comprising 10k hours of egocentric human data and 3k hours of robot data with unified multimodal annotations and systematic quality control. A unified kinematic representation encodes locomotion through camera poses and manipulation through projected skeletons, with robot skeletons combining embodiment-specific forward kinematics with extensive manual keypoint annotation and correction. We also introduce Xp-Teleop, a long-horizon loco-manipulation benchmark based on high-quality dexterous humanoid teleoperation data. Evaluations demonstrate state-of-the-art performance across five cross-embodiment benchmarks (DreamDojo, Ψ_0, ω-HOME, Xp-Teleop, and AgiBot) and on held-out human egocentric video, from zero-shot inference to few-shot and full-data post-training. Scaling human pre-training data improves performance on both human and robot evaluations. After distillation, our model supports real-time, minute-long rollouts, enabling live VR interaction. Applications in policy evaluation, model-based planning, and world-action modeling further demonstrate the model's utility for embodied decision-making.

ru.title: Один мир для людей и роботов: единая модель движения и манипуляций
ru.desc: Ropedia W0 — это фундаментальная world-модель (World Foundation Model) для совместного обучения locomotion и manipulation на данных людей и роботов с разными телами. Авторы собрали датасет Xp-Data (10 тысяч часов egocentric-видео людей и 3 тысячи часов роботов) с единой мультимодальной разметкой и контролем качества. Действия кодируются через унифицированное кинематическое представление: перемещение описывается позами камеры, манипуляции — спроецированными скелетами, а для роботов используется forward kinematics вместе с ручной разметкой ключевых точек. Модель достигает state-of-the-art результатов на пяти кросс-эмбодимент бенчмарках, работает в реальном времени и полезна для оценки политик, планирования и моделирования действий.

en.title: Unifying Human and Robot Loco-Manipulation with Ropedia W0
en.desc: Ropedia W0 is a groundbreaking foundation model designed for loco-manipulation, integrating data from both humans and robots through a unified kinematic framework. It addresses the complexities of joint locomotion and manipulation by utilizing a large dataset called Xp-Data, which includes extensive egocentric human and robot data with detailed annotations. The model achieves impressive results across multiple benchmarks, showcasing its ability to perform zero-shot and few-shot learning effectively. Additionally, Ropedia W0 supports real-time interactions in virtual reality, making it valuable for applications in policy evaluation and decision-making in embodied systems.

zh.title: 跨体现运动操控的基础模型
zh.desc: Ropedia W0 是一个跨体现的运动操控基础模型，能够统一人类和机器人数据，通过运动学表示实现了在多个基准测试中的最佳性能。该模型使用了10,000小时的人类数据和3,000小时的机器人数据，提供了统一的多模态注释和系统质量控制。通过相机姿态编码运动，通过投影骨架编码操控，结合了特定体现的前向运动学和手动关键点注释。我们的模型支持实时的长时间滚动，能够用于虚拟现实交互，并在政策评估和基于模型的规划等应用中展现出其在体现决策中的实用性。

papers.title: PAR: Progress-Aligned Recurrence for Length Generalization in State Tracking
papers.abstract: Abstract Progress-Aligned Recurrence trains looped language models to match intermediate states and stabilize recurrent norms, enabling strong length extrapolation on sequential tracking tasks.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Looped language models can run more iterations at test time, but additional iterations need not help them solve longer problems. For sequential state tracking, final-answer supervision does not specify how far each iteration should advance, and repeated updates can change the scale of the recurrent state. We introduce Progress-Aligned Recurrence (PAR), which trains the prediction at iteration k to match the state after the first k operations and rescales recurrent states to their first-iteration norms. On swap-S_5, a Qwen2.5-0.5B model trained on at most 32 moves achieves 95.5\% mean full-state accuracy at 512 moves, or 16times the training length, compared with 55.7\% reported for RLT and 0.8\% for explicit chain of thought on the same backbone. Controlled S_5 ablations show that removing norm anchoring reduces the extrapolation factor from 16times to below 2.2times, and replacing progress-aligned targets with final-answer supervision reduces it to at most 8times. A learned completion readout selects when to answer without a supplied stopping depth. When intermediate labels are unavailable, prefix self-distillation induces the correspondence from shorter problem prefixes using only final answers. The gains apply across sequential state-tracking tasks, establishing the task structure required for depth extrapolation. These findings support training intermediate predictions and state scale together to make additional recurrent depth useful for longer problems.

ru.title: Учим рекуррентную модель идти шаг за шагом и не терять масштаб
ru.desc: Статья предлагает метод Progress-Aligned Recurrence (PAR) для looped language models, то есть рекуррентных LLM, которые могут выполнять больше итераций на этапе инференса. Идея в том, что на каждой итерации k предсказание обучается соответствовать состоянию после первых k операций, а норма рекуррентного состояния нормализуется к норме первой итерации. На задаче отслеживания состояний swap-S_5 модель, обученная максимум на 32 ходах, достигает 95.5% точности на 512 ходах, что примерно в 16 раз больше длины обучения. Абляции показывают, что и выравнивание по прогрессу, и нормализация масштаба состояния критичны для экстраполяции по глубине, а prefix self-distillation позволяет обойтись без промежуточных разметок.

en.title: Enhancing Language Models with Progress-Aligned Recurrence
en.desc: This paper introduces Progress-Aligned Recurrence (PAR), a method that enhances looped language models by aligning their intermediate states during training. PAR allows models to better handle longer sequential tasks by ensuring that each iteration's prediction corresponds to the state after the first k operations. The approach stabilizes recurrent norms, which helps the model maintain accuracy even when extrapolating beyond its training length. The results show significant improvements in performance on sequential tracking tasks, demonstrating the importance of training with intermediate predictions and state scaling.

zh.title: 进度对齐递归：提升循环模型的序列跟踪能力
zh.desc: 本文提出了一种名为进度对齐递归（Progress-Aligned Recurrence, PAR）的方法，用于训练循环语言模型，以匹配中间状态并稳定递归规范。这种方法使得模型在处理序列跟踪任务时能够有效地进行长度外推。通过将每次迭代的预测与前k次操作后的状态对齐，PAR能够提高模型在长问题上的表现。实验结果表明，使用PAR的模型在512步的任务中达到了95.5%的准确率，显著优于传统方法。

papers.title: S-Agent 2.0: Spatial Reasoning with a General Coding Agent
papers.abstract: Abstract S-Agent 2.0 improves spatial reasoning by integrating a persistent scene memory and plain-language interpretation into a coding agent with 3D perception tools.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Spatial reasoning asks a model to work out where objects are in 3D space, how they relate to one another, and how they move. Agentic VLMs have recently brought large improvements on such tasks by letting the model actively gather evidence with 3D perception tools instead of answering in a single pass. Even so, on many questions the tools return the right evidence and the model still does not arrive at the correct answer: the gap between model and tools, where raw readings become usable conclusions, is left unfilled. We present S-Agent 2.0, a spatial reasoning agent that equips an off-the-shelf general coding agent with a command-line perception toolkit, and we design the interface around one principle: help the VLM close the evidence loop: acquire scene evidence, remember it in a persistent scene memory, and interpret each reading in plain spatial language. This design keeps the full flexibility of a coding agent, and every reading it acts on stays grounded in the tools' geometry. On MMSI-Bench and ReVSI, the toolkit improves a strong open-source model, Qwen3.8-27B, by +13.9 and +20.5 points over the same agent without tools, and a strong closed-source model, Gemini-3.8-Flash, by +11.2 and +9.6 points. With the open backbone S-Agent 2.0 reaches 66.5 on MMSI-Bench and 82.3 on ReVSI, ahead of the specialized system SpatialClaw on the same backbone (62.6 and 74.5), and with Gemini-3.8-Flash it reaches 74.1 and 90.5 against its 67.0 and 79.7. Both tool gains shrink as the backbone grows more capable, but SpatialClaw's shrinks far more on ReVSI, from +13.2 to +2.7, while ours stays at +9.6. S-Agent 2.0 also works across different general coding agent harnesses, such as Codex and Claude Code.

ru.title: От сырых измерений к пространственному пониманию: замыкаем цикл доказательств
ru.desc: Статья представляет S-Agent 2.0 — агента для пространственного рассуждения, построенного на базе универсального coding agent с набором инструментов 3D-восприятия через командную строку. Ключевая идея: помочь VLM замкнуть цикл доказательств, то есть собирать данные о сцене, хранить их в персистентной памяти сцены и интерпретировать показания на простом пространственном языке. На бенчмарках MMSI-Bench и ReVSI инструменты заметно повышают качество моделей Qwen3.8-27B и Gemini-3.8-Flash, а открытая версия превосходит специализированную систему SpatialClaw. Подход также работает с разными coding agent harness, такими как Codex и Claude Code.

en.title: Closing the Evidence Loop in Spatial Reasoning
en.desc: S-Agent 2.0 enhances spatial reasoning in machine learning by combining a persistent scene memory with plain-language interpretation, allowing a coding agent to utilize 3D perception tools effectively. This model addresses the challenge of translating raw spatial data into actionable conclusions, thereby closing the evidence loop in spatial reasoning tasks. By integrating a command-line perception toolkit, S-Agent 2.0 enables the agent to gather, remember, and interpret spatial evidence dynamically. The results show significant performance improvements on benchmark tests, outperforming both open-source and closed-source models in spatial reasoning tasks.

zh.title: 提升空间推理能力的智能代理
zh.desc: S-Agent 2.0 是一种空间推理代理，通过整合持久场景记忆和自然语言解释，提升了3D感知工具的编码能力。该模型能够在3D空间中识别物体的位置、相互关系及其运动方式。与传统模型不同，S-Agent 2.0 允许模型主动收集证据，从而更好地理解和解释场景信息。实验结果显示，S-Agent 2.0 在多个基准测试中显著提高了性能，展示了其在空间推理任务中的优势。

papers.title: Sage-A1.5: From Long-Horizon Execution to Scientific Exploration with Capability Composition
papers.abstract: Abstract Sage-A1.5 is a 35B mixture-of-experts agentic model that improves long-horizon problem solving via adaptive task delegation, verification, and open scientific exploration.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small In this report, we introduce Sage-A1.5, a 35B Mixture-of-Experts agentic model that builds on A1 to advance long-horizon problem solving through adaptive capability composition. Compared with A1, Sage-A1.5 learns not only to solve individual tasks, but also to organize work and revise its approach during execution. Sage-A1.5 highlights three improvements: agentic orchestration, verification, and open scientific discovery. First, agentic orchestration extends single-agent execution through task delegation and parallel collaboration among subagents with isolated contexts, enabling complex tasks to be decomposed and addressed concurrently and supporting efficient execution while reducing interference across concurrent subagents. Second, agentic verification strengthens long-horizon reliability through progress checking, evidence validation, and reflective strategy revision, allowing the agent to recognize unproductive search paths and pursue alternative approaches. Third, open scientific discovery extends agentic capabilities beyond answering predefined questions to conducting exploratory research, connecting scientific inquiry with interactive analysis and inspectable research artifacts. We showcase these capabilities through complicated agentic tasks and multidisciplinary scientific applications. Besides, we hope Sage-A1.5 provides the community with an accessible foundation for open scientific discovery, offering a practical path from long-horizon task execution to collaborative, verifiable, and inspectable scientific exploration.

ru.title: Агентный AI, который сам организует работу и проверяет себя в открытых научных исследованиях
ru.desc: В статье представлена Sage-A1.5 — агентная LLM на базе архитектуры Mixture-of-Experts с 35 миллиардами параметров, развивающая предыдущую модель A1. Ключевые улучшения: агентная оркестрация, при которой задачи делегируются параллельным субагентам с изолированным контекстом, и механизм верификации с проверкой прогресса, валидацией доказательств и рефлексивной сменой стратегии. Модель также расширяется до открытых научных исследований, где AI не только отвечает на заранее заданные вопросы, но и самостоятельно проводит исследовательский анализ с проверяемыми артефактами. Авторы демонстрируют эффективность на сложных агентных задачах и междисциплинарных научных приложениях и надеются, что модель станет доступной основой для открытых научных открытий.

en.title: Empowering Long-Horizon Problem Solving with Sage-A1.5
en.desc: Sage-A1.5 is a 35 billion parameter mixture-of-experts model designed to enhance long-term problem solving by allowing adaptive task delegation and verification. It improves upon its predecessor, A1, by not only solving tasks but also organizing and adjusting its methods during execution. The model features agentic orchestration for efficient task management among subagents, agentic verification for ensuring reliability through progress checks, and open scientific discovery for conducting exploratory research. This framework aims to facilitate complex tasks and promote collaborative scientific exploration, making it a valuable resource for the research community.

zh.title: Sage-A1.5：智能任务委派与科学探索的未来
zh.desc: Sage-A1.5是一种35B的混合专家模型，旨在通过自适应任务委派、验证和开放科学探索来改善长期问题解决能力。与之前的A1模型相比，Sage-A1.5不仅能够解决单个任务，还能在执行过程中组织工作和修正方法。该模型的三个主要改进包括代理协调、验证和开放科学发现，能够支持复杂任务的并行处理和高效执行。通过这些能力，Sage-A1.5为科学探索提供了一个可访问的基础，促进了从长期任务执行到可验证的科学研究的转变。

papers.title: CoEvo-RSI: When Harnesses Evolve, Which Models Should Follow?
papers.abstract: Abstract CoEvo-RSI reduces brain-body mismatch in recursive self-improving agents by using bidirectional historical inheritance to align model capabilities with evolving harness requirements, achieving strong results via supervised fine-tuning.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Model--harness co-evolution has emerged as a prominent paradigm for recursive self-improving (RSI) agents, jointly evolving their execution scaffolds and intrinsic capabilities. We study the persistent yet often overlooked brain--body mismatch problem in this paradigm, where an evolving harness (body) demands behaviors its model (brain) has not learned or restricts capabilities it already possesses. We introduce CoEvo-RSI, a RSI framework that advances model--harness co-evolution through agent-driven, bidirectional historical inheritance. Drawing on a shared evolutionary archive and execution feedback, a meta-agent coordinates harness development from historical designs with model checkpoint selection or merging and subsequent adaptation under the selected harness, aligning inherited capabilities with evolving execution requirements to reduce brain--body mismatch. Using only supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on its own rejection-sampled trajectories, CoEvo-RSI makes Qwen3.5-9B competitive with larger models across diverse vertical applications, including multi-agent failure attribution, role-aware text-to-SQL, and smart-home instruction following. It surpasses DeepSeek-V4-Pro on TraceElephant (+14.16 agent accuracy) and GLM-5.3 on HomeBench VM (+4.90 success rate), underscoring the need for brain--body alignment and the potential of bidirectional historical inheritance to advance agent co-evolution.

ru.title: Согласуй мозг с телом — и маленькая модель обгонит гигантов
ru.desc: В статье предлагается CoEvo-RSI — фреймворк для рекурсивно самоулучшающихся агентов, в котором модель (brain) и harness (body) совместно эволюционируют. Авторы вводят двунаправленное наследование истории из общего эволюционного архива, а meta-agent выбирает архитектуру harness и checkpoint модели или их merging с последующей адаптацией. Обучение ведётся только через SFT на собственных rejection-sampled траекториях, что позволяет Qwen3.5-9B конкурировать с гораздо более крупными LLM. Модель превосходит DeepSeek-V4-Pro на TraceElephant и GLM-5.3 на HomeBench VM, что подчёркивает важность согласования brain и body.

en.title: Aligning Brain and Body for Smarter Agents
en.desc: The paper introduces CoEvo-RSI, a framework designed to address the brain-body mismatch problem in recursive self-improving (RSI) agents. It utilizes bidirectional historical inheritance to ensure that the capabilities of the model (brain) align with the evolving requirements of its harness (body). By leveraging a shared evolutionary archive and execution feedback, CoEvo-RSI coordinates the development of the harness while adapting the model to meet these requirements. The framework demonstrates strong performance through supervised fine-tuning, outperforming larger models in various applications, highlighting the importance of aligning model capabilities with harness demands.

zh.title: 大脑与身体的完美协调
zh.desc: CoEvo-RSI是一种递归自我改进代理的框架，旨在减少大脑与身体之间的不匹配问题。它通过双向历史继承来协调模型能力与不断发展的执行需求，从而提高代理的表现。该方法利用共享的进化档案和执行反馈，确保模型的能力与身体的需求相一致。通过仅使用监督微调，CoEvo-RSI使得Qwen3.5-9B在多个应用中表现出色，超越了其他大型模型。

papers.title: VLA-Rolling: Fewer Denoising Steps, Better Control via Adaptive Action Reuse
papers.abstract: Abstract VLA-Rolling improves vision-language-action model efficiency by reusing discarded action tails with adaptive denoising budgets, reducing inference cost and boosting success rates.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Flow-matching vision-language-action (VLA) models generate an action chunk by iteratively denoising Gaussian noise, but typically execute only a short prefix before replanning with updated observations. Under this receding-horizon paradigm, the unexecuted remainder---the action tail---is discarded, and the next chunk is regenerated from fresh noise. We show that this discarded tail retains transferable denoising progress: action-tail initialization can match or outperform a native 10-step Gaussian baseline using fewer denoising steps. However, the optimal denoising budget varies substantially across samples, indicating that tail reuse should be adapted to the updated environment. Based on this observation, we introduce VLA-Rolling, a lightweight inference framework that reuses action tails through three stages: action-tail inheritance, per-action confidence estimation, and confidence-guided refinement through renoising and denoising budget allocation, while the underlying VLA remains frozen. Across π_{0.5}, SmolVLA, X-VLA, and MolmoAct2 on LIBERO, MetaWorld, LIBERO-Plus, and RoboTwin 2.0, VLA-Rolling reduces action-chunk inference cost in all 16 model--benchmark pairs, achieving up to a 1.48times speedup, while improving success rate in 14 pairs by up to 15.08 percentage points. These results show that action tails are not merely discarded predictions, but reusable intermediate states that enable more efficient and accurate VLA inference. These results demonstrate that the action tail can support the generation of better actions with fewer denoising steps. Our project is available at https://chenbao123ww.github.io/VLA-Rolling/.
affiliations: OmniAI Group of ZJU ACES Lab

ru.title: Не выбрасывай хвост действий: переиспользуй его для более быстрых и точных решений
ru.desc: Авторы предлагают VLA-Rolling — лёгкий фреймворк для ускорения flow-matching VLA-моделей, замороженных при инференсе. Вместо того чтобы выбрасывать невыполненную часть action chunk (action tail), метод переиспользует её как промежуточное состояние для инициализации следующего денойзинга. Бюджет шагов денойзинга адаптивно выбирается по per-action confidence, а уточнение выполняется через renoising. На LIBERO, MetaWorld, LIBERO-Plus и RoboTwin 2.0 метод снижает стоимость инференса до 1.48x и повышает success rate в большинстве случаев.

en.title: Maximizing Efficiency by Reusing Action Tails in VLA Models
en.desc: The paper introduces VLA-Rolling, a method that enhances the efficiency of vision-language-action (VLA) models by reusing previously discarded action tails. These action tails, which are the unexecuted parts of planned actions, can be adapted and reused to improve the model's performance without starting from scratch. By implementing a framework that includes action-tail inheritance and confidence-guided refinement, VLA-Rolling reduces the computational cost of generating actions while increasing the success rates of the models. The results show significant improvements across various benchmarks, demonstrating that action tails can be valuable resources rather than just wasted predictions.

zh.title: 重用动作尾部，提升模型效率
zh.desc: VLA-Rolling是一种提高视觉-语言-动作模型效率的方法，通过重用被丢弃的动作尾部并采用自适应去噪预算，降低推理成本并提高成功率。传统的VLA模型在生成动作时，通常只执行短暂的前缀，然后根据更新的观察重新规划，导致未执行的动作尾部被丢弃。研究表明，这些被丢弃的动作尾部保留了可转移的去噪进展，可以通过重用这些尾部来提高效率。VLA-Rolling通过三个阶段实现动作尾部的重用，显著减少了推理成本并提高了成功率，证明了动作尾部是可重用的中间状态。

papers.title: SolarRenderer: Few-Step Generative Reference Rendering
papers.abstract: Abstract SolarRenderer adapts a frozen video backbone with lightweight LoRAs to render realistic videos from diverse structural inputs in four steps or real-time streaming, using frame-aligned training data.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Game engines and coding agents can specify the layout, motion, and camera of a scene, yet turning such coarse structure into realistic video requires a renderer that follows the structure and completes the appearance it leaves open. Existing renderers are tied to the representation of one engine, need tens of denoising steps or a costly distillation of their own, and learn from conditions that are not aligned with their target videos. We present SolarRenderer, a structure-conditioned video renderer that adapts a frozen MiniMax-H3 33B backbone with two lightweight LoRAs. Structural videos enter the native reference pathway of the backbone at the positions of the frames they describe, without a type identifier and described only in plain text, so that a single control LoRA follows arbitrary structural representations. Starting from a pretrained four-step LoRA, structure-guided distribution matching renders in four steps, 12.3 times faster than 50-step sampling, while preserving the learned control. A block-causal variant extends the same design to streaming and renders 768p video in real time. To train the model, we build a frame-aligned corpus of 136K clips from game engines, simulators, and YouTube videos. Experiments on an in-distribution test set and a generalization benchmark of 16 structural representations show that SolarRenderer achieves state-of-the-art results across both, and generalizes to 11 unseen representations, including pose skeletons, drawings, and point clouds.

ru.title: Структура на входе, реалистичное видо на выходе за четыре шага
ru.desc: SolarRenderer — это модель для генерации реалистичного видео по структурным входным данным, таким как раскладка сцены, движение и положение камеры из игровых движков. Она адаптирует замороженный видео-бэкбон MiniMax-H3 33B с помощью двух легковесных LoRA, подавая структурные видео напрямую в нативный reference-путь модели без указания типа входа. Благодаря structure-guided distribution matching рендеринг занимает четыре шага вместо пятидесяти и в 12.3 раза быстрее, а block-causal вариант позволяет стриминг в 768p в реальном времени. Модель обучена на корпусе из 136K выровненных по кадрам клипов и показывает state-of-the-art результаты, обобщаясь даже на неизвестные представления вроде скелетов поз, рисунков и облаков точек.

en.title: Transforming Structure into Realistic Video at Lightning Speed
en.desc: SolarRenderer is a novel video rendering system that utilizes a frozen MiniMax-H3 33B backbone enhanced with lightweight LoRAs to create realistic videos from various structural inputs. It operates in four steps, significantly speeding up the rendering process to 12.3 times faster than traditional methods while maintaining high-quality output. The model is trained on a large dataset of 136K clips, ensuring it can generalize well to different structural representations, including pose skeletons and drawings. By integrating structure-guided distribution matching, SolarRenderer effectively transforms coarse structural descriptions into detailed video content in real-time.

zh.title: 快速生成逼真视频的结构条件渲染器
zh.desc: SolarRenderer是一种结构条件的视频渲染器，它利用冻结的MiniMax-H3 33B骨干网和轻量级的LoRA来生成逼真的视频。该模型通过四个步骤快速渲染视频，速度比传统的50步采样快12.3倍，同时保持学习到的控制能力。SolarRenderer能够处理来自游戏引擎、模拟器和YouTube视频的结构化输入，并在多种结构表示上实现了最先进的结果。实验表明，该模型不仅在已知数据集上表现优异，还能很好地推广到未见过的结构表示。

papers.title: Learning the 4D World through Point Trajectory Forecasting
papers.abstract: Abstract Video-Point Model predicts future multi-view videos and 3D point trajectories from video histories and instructions, improving forecasting and robot control through shared 3D-aware representations.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Reliable multi-view forecasting requires videos from different cameras to describe the same evolving 3D scene. To this end, we introduce Video-Point Model (VPM), a world model that conditions on multi-view video histories and a language instruction to jointly forecast future videos from arbitrary viewpoints and the 3D trajectories of persistent scene points. We extend a pretrained world model with camera-conditioned multi-view processing that integrates complementary observations across cameras, and add a trajectory head that predicts how physical points move through time. Each trajectory tracks a single point across all views, and supervising these trajectories alongside video generation therefore anchors appearance changes in every camera to a shared description of 3D motion. To support training and evaluation, we build VPM-Data, a simulation corpus pairing synchronized multi-view videos with persistent point trajectories, and VP-WorldBench, a forecasting benchmark spanning simulated and real environments. We further extend VPM to robot control by adding robot actions as a token modality in the generator. Action tokens share the point-supervised backbone and are denoised jointly with future videos, thereby grounding the policy in the same 3D-aware representation. On VP-WorldBench and existing 4D generation benchmarks, point supervision improves both video fidelity and 3D motion accuracy over a video-only counterpart, and in simulated and real-robot experiments, it also raises the manipulation success of the action-enabled model.

ru.title: Видим сцену в 3D — предсказываем её будущее и управляем роботом
ru.desc: Авторы представляют Video-Point Model (VPM) — world model, которая по истории многокамерного видео и языковой инструкции одновременно предсказывает будущие видео с произвольных ракурсов и 3D-траектории постоянных точек сцены. Модель расширяет предобученный backbone механизмом camera-conditioned multi-view обработки и дополнительной trajectory head, а обучение на траекториях точек связывает изменения внешнего вида во всех камерах с единым описанием 3D-движения. Для обучения и оценки создан датасет VPM-Data из синхронизированных симуляционных видео и VP-WorldBench для прогнозирования в симулированных и реальных средах. Расширение моделью действий робота как токенов позволяет использовать ту же 3D-aware представление для управления роботом, что повышает точность движения и успешность манипуляций.

en.title: Predicting Future Videos and 3D Motion with Video-Point Model
en.desc: The Video-Point Model (VPM) is designed to predict future multi-view videos and 3D point trajectories by utilizing historical video data and language instructions. It integrates multi-view processing to enhance the understanding of a 3D scene from different camera angles, allowing for accurate forecasting of future events. By supervising the movement of physical points across various views, VPM ensures that changes in appearance are linked to a consistent 3D motion description. Additionally, VPM is extended for robot control, enabling it to incorporate action tokens that improve the model's ability to perform tasks in both simulated and real environments.

zh.title: 视频点模型：提升多视角视频预测与机器人控制的未来
zh.desc: 视频点模型（Video-Point Model, VPM）通过结合多视角视频历史和语言指令，预测未来的视频和三维点轨迹，从而提升了预测精度和机器人控制能力。该模型利用预训练的世界模型，整合来自不同摄像头的互补观察，能够共同预测任意视角下的未来视频和持久场景点的三维轨迹。每个轨迹跟踪一个点在所有视角中的运动，并通过视频生成监督这些轨迹，从而将每个摄像头的外观变化与共享的三维运动描述相结合。通过构建VPM-Data和VP-WorldBench，我们为训练和评估提供了同步的多视角视频和持久点轨迹的模拟数据集。

papers.title: Correction Training for Diffusion Models
papers.abstract: Abstract A correction module trained to refine diffusion predictions reduces exposure bias, improving unguided sample quality and enabling distillation to eliminate inference overhead.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Iterative sampling in diffusion models can lead to error accumulation due to exposure bias. The denoiser is trained on real images interpolated with noise, but at inference its inputs are constructed from its own imperfect predictions from the earlier steps, something it has never seen at training time. This might be one reason diffusion models often struggle without additional help, such as CFG. We introduce a correction step for diffusion models which attempts to reduce this training-inference gap. The corrector takes the base model's prediction as input and is trained against the same ground-truth target. This makes correction an explicit learning task, with training inputs provided by the base model. During sampling, at each denoising step, we iteratively refine the denoiser's clean-sample prediction. This allows us to correct predictions at intermediate denoising steps, preventing early artifacts from persisting into the final sample. Although the corrector is trained only on predictions from the base denoiser, it can be applied repeatedly to its own outputs at inference for better results. This simple framework leads to substantial improvement in sample quality while largely preserving diversity. We evaluate our method across DiT, SiT, and JiT. Our method substantially improves upon previously reported FID scores for unguided generation and, notably, unconditional generation, where producing high-quality samples without guidance has been particularly challenging. Our method achieves performance competitive with classifier-free guidance (CFG), and combining correction with CFG further improves diversity and reduces oversaturation typical of CFG. Finally, we show that the additional inference cost of correction can be amortized by distilling the refined predictions back into the base diffusion model, retaining the quality gains without additional inference-time overhead.

ru.title: Исправляем ошибки диффузии на лету, чтобы картинки стали чище без CFG
ru.desc: Авторы предлагают корректирующий модуль для диффузионных моделей, который уменьшает эффект exposure bias, то есть разрыв между обучением и инференсом, когда модель получает на вход собственные неидеальные предсказания. Корректор обучается на предсказаниях базовой модели с тем же ground-truth таргетом и итеративно уточняет чистое предсказание на каждом шаге денойзинга. Метод заметно улучшает качество генерации без guidance, включая безусловную генерацию, и даёт результаты, сопоставимые с CFG, при этом сохраняя разнообразие. Дополнительные вычисления на инференсе устраняются дистилляцией уточнённых предсказаний обратно в базовую модель.

en.title: Refining Diffusion Predictions for Better Sample Quality
en.desc: This paper presents a correction module designed to enhance the predictions made by diffusion models, addressing the issue of exposure bias that can degrade sample quality. By training the corrector on the base model's predictions, it explicitly learns to refine these outputs, thereby reducing errors that accumulate during iterative sampling. The approach allows for improved unguided sample generation, achieving better performance metrics like FID scores, especially in unconditional generation scenarios. Additionally, the method can be integrated with classifier-free guidance to further enhance diversity and quality without incurring significant inference costs.

zh.title: 修正模块提升扩散模型样本质量
zh.desc: 本文提出了一种修正模块，用于改善扩散模型的预测，减少曝光偏差，从而提高无指导样本的质量。该修正步骤通过将基础模型的预测作为输入，并针对真实目标进行训练，形成了一个明确的学习任务。在采样过程中，我们在每个去噪步骤中迭代地优化去噪器的预测，防止早期伪影影响最终样本。实验结果表明，该方法在无指导生成和无条件生成任务中显著提高了样本质量，同时保持了多样性。

papers.title: SWIFT: Self-guided Weak-to-strong dIFfusion models via Target extrapolation
papers.abstract: Abstract Swift improves diffusion model training by extrapolating regression targets away from a frozen weak denoiser, reducing error and training cost without inference overhead.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Training high-quality diffusion models is computationally expensive, and inference-time guidance often adds further sampling cost. In this work, we introduce Swift, a simple yet effective self-guided training method that uses a frozen weak denoiser to improve a stronger model without adding inference overhead. For each noisy input, Swift extrapolates the clean regression target away from the weak denoiser's prediction, amplifying components that remain underfit. The weak guide can be an early training checkpoint, requires no backpropagation during main-model training, and is discarded afterward. The resulting model retains the original sampler and supports both conditional and unconditional generation without label dropout or an unconditional branch. We explain this mechanism through a spectral analysis of finite-time population gradient flow in an RKHS. With an early-stopped weak guide, we prove that a nonempty range of extrapolation strengths yields strictly lower posterior-mean error than matched standard training, despite shifting the regression target away from the posterior mean. Experiments on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-256 demonstrate improvements across model scales and representations. In one ImageNet-256 configuration, Swift surpasses the baseline's best FID using roughly half the total training compute, including guide preparation and training overhead. On RAEv2, it achieves FID 1.15 without inference-time guidance and 0.99 with guidance. These results establish target extrapolation as an effective approach to weak-to-strong diffusion training with efficient single-model inference.

ru.title: Экстраполяция цели обучения: быстрее и лучше диффузионные модели без лишних затрат на инференс
ru.desc: В статье предлагается метод Swift, который ускоряет обучение диффузионных моделей без дополнительных затрат на инференс. Во время обучения регрессионная цель сдвигается от предсказания замороженного слабого денойзера, что усиливает компоненты, недообученные основной моделью. Авторы теоретически показывают на основе спектрального анализа в RKHS, что при определённой силе экстраполяции ошибка оценки апостериорного среднего ниже, чем при стандартном обучении. Эксперименты на CIFAR-10 и ImageNet-256 подтверждают улучшение FID при меньших вычислительных затратах.

en.title: Swift: Efficient Training for Stronger Diffusion Models
en.desc: The paper introduces Swift, a novel training method for diffusion models that enhances performance while reducing computational costs. By using a frozen weak denoiser, Swift extrapolates regression targets to improve the training of a stronger model without increasing inference time. This approach allows for better fitting of underrepresented components in the data, leading to lower error rates compared to traditional training methods. Experiments show that Swift achieves superior results on datasets like CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-256, demonstrating its effectiveness in efficient model training and inference.

zh.title: Swift：高效的扩散模型训练方法
zh.desc: Swift是一种改进扩散模型训练的方法，通过从一个冻结的弱去噪器中推导回归目标，降低了误差和训练成本，而不增加推理开销。该方法利用弱去噪器的预测来推导干净的回归目标，放大那些仍然未被充分拟合的部分。Swift不需要在主模型训练期间进行反向传播，且在训练后可以丢弃弱去噪器。实验结果表明，Swift在多个模型规模和表示上均有显著提升，尤其在ImageNet-256上表现优异。

papers.title: MMEnterprise-Bench: Evaluating Enterprise Agents over Evolving Multimodal Records
papers.abstract: Abstract MMEnterprise-Bench evaluates multimodal agents on reasoning over evolving workplace records with conflicts and missing evidence.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Enterprise agents answer questions over workplace records that evolve through team collaboration. As information is shared, corrected, and revised across documents, chats, and figures, multiple versions of the same information accumulate in the workspace. Reliable question answering therefore requires agents to reason over sufficient evidence, resolve cross-source and temporal conflicts, and recognize when the available evidence is insufficient to establish an answer. To systematically evaluate these capabilities, we introduce MMEnterprise-Bench, a benchmark comprising 1,613 questions grounded in evolving multimodal records from simulated collaboration projects, covering three categories: Evidence Reasoning, Conflict Resolution, and Unanswerability. We evaluate 10 proprietary and open-source multimodal LLMs and find that even the strongest models struggle when evidence contains cross-source or temporal conflicts or spans multiple images. Moreover, increasing the retrieval budget or employing a larger retriever improves evidence recall but does not consistently translate into higher answer accuracy. These findings highlight the persistent challenges of reasoning over evolving workplace records and establish MMEnterprise-Bench as a testbed for developing more reliable enterprise agents. Code and data are available at https://mlvlab.github.io/MMEnterprise-Bench/.
affiliations: Korea University, Seoul, Republic of Korea

ru.title: Корпоративные AI-агенты пока не умеют разбираться в противоречивых данных
ru.desc: Авторы представляют MMEnterprise-Bench — бенчмарк для оценки мультимодальных AI-агентов, которые отвечают на вопросы по корпоративным рабочим записям, постоянно меняющимся в ходе командной работы. Набор содержит 1613 вопросов по трём категориям: Evidence Reasoning, Conflict Resolution и Unanswerability, где агент должен распознать недостаточность данных. Протестированы 10 мультимодальных LLM, и даже лучшие модели плохо справляются с конфликтами между источниками, временными противоречиями и несколькими изображениями. Показано, что увеличение бюджета retrieval или более крупный retriever повышает полноту найденных доказательств, но не всегда улучшает точность ответов.

en.title: Evaluating Multimodal Agents in Evolving Workspaces
en.desc: The paper introduces MMEnterprise-Bench, a benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal agents on their ability to reason over evolving workplace records that may contain conflicts and missing information. It focuses on how these agents can answer questions based on documents, chats, and figures that change over time due to team collaboration. The benchmark includes 1,613 questions that assess three key areas: Evidence Reasoning, Conflict Resolution, and Unanswerability. The study reveals that even advanced multimodal language models struggle with cross-source conflicts and temporal discrepancies, emphasizing the need for improved reasoning capabilities in enterprise agents.

zh.title: 提升多模态智能体的推理能力
zh.desc: MMEnterprise-Bench 是一个评估多模态智能体在处理不断变化的工作记录时的推理能力的基准。该基准包含 1,613 个问题，涉及证据推理、冲突解决和无法回答性等三个类别。研究发现，即使是最强大的模型，在处理跨来源或时间冲突的证据时也会遇到困难。此外，增加检索预算或使用更大的检索器可以提高证据的召回率，但并不总能提高答案的准确性。

papers.title: Joints, Camera, Action! Co-Generating 3D Motion and Video for Arbitrary Rigs
papers.abstract: Abstract The model co-generates video and 3D motion for arbitrary skeletons via cross-attention with a pretrained video generator, enabling scene-registered animation and bidirectional video-motion conversion.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Video generation models can now depict remarkably realistic motion. Yet it is unclear how to use this motion beyond pixels: to animate a specific 3D asset and replay the animation in its 3D scene. For instance, a video model can show a monkey jumping over a crossbar, but it cannot return that jump as replayable 3D motion placed in the 3D scene. Here we present a model that directly co-generates the video and 3D motion for any supplied rig, along with a camera that registers this motion to the scene. Prior video-motion models either handle only human skeletons, often adding billions of parameters, or triangulate 3D motion from generated 2D pose maps. We instead keep 3D motion in a separate model that supports arbitrary skeletons, and connect it to a pretrained video model through a small set of cross-attention layers. This separation lets the motion model first learn how skeletons move from motion-only data, which is easier to obtain and augment than paired video. Additionally, our model learns to locate each joint in the video frames, which lets us recover the camera and place the 3D motion in the scene. To train across many skeletons, we use a generative video editor to place animated 3D assets in scenes suited to their actions, curating the edits so their known motion remains valid. Together with human and robot video, this yields nearly 200K training pairs. Our evaluations demonstrate that our model animates diverse rigs from text more faithfully than video-first pipelines, and its motion responds to the surrounding scene. It also turns video into rig motion, rig motion into video, and enables keyframe-based control of the 3D motion. Videos and additional results are available on our project page: https://research.nvidia.com/labs/par/projects/jca/.

ru.title: Одна модель рисует видео и 3D-движение сразу, привязывая его к сцене
ru.desc: Статья представляет модель, которая одновременно генерирует видео и 3D-движение для произвольного скелета (rig) и восстанавливает камеру, чтобы привязать движение к сцене. Вместо того чтобы ограничиваться человеческими скелетами или триангулировать 3D-позы из 2D, авторы держат 3D-движение в отдельной модели и соединяют её с предобученным video generation моделью через небольшой набор cross-attention слоёв. Такое разделение позволяет обучать модель движения на motion-only данных, которые проще получить, чем парные видео, а для обучения на множестве скелетов используется generative video editor и около 200K обучающих пар. Модель превосходит video-first пайплайны по точности анимации и умеет конвертировать видео в движение rig и обратно, а также управлять движением по keyframes.

en.title: Bridging Video and 3D Motion for Any Skeleton
en.desc: This paper presents a novel model that generates both video and 3D motion for any skeleton using cross-attention with a pretrained video generator. Unlike previous models that are limited to human skeletons or require extensive parameters, this approach allows for arbitrary skeletons and separates the 3D motion learning from video generation. The model effectively learns joint locations in video frames, enabling accurate placement of 3D animations in their respective scenes. By utilizing a large dataset of nearly 200K training pairs, the model demonstrates superior performance in animating diverse rigs and converting between video and rig motion.

zh.title: 视频与3D运动的双向生成模型
zh.desc: 该论文提出了一种新模型，可以同时生成视频和3D运动，适用于任意骨架。通过与预训练的视频生成器进行交叉注意力，该模型能够实现场景注册动画和双向视频-运动转换。与以往只能处理人类骨架的模型不同，该模型支持任意骨架，并通过少量交叉注意力层与视频模型连接。我们的评估表明，该模型能够更真实地从文本生成多样的动画，并且其运动能够响应周围场景。

papers.title: LLM2R: From Large Language Models to 3D Reassemblers
papers.abstract: Abstract LLM2R treats 3D part assembly as sequence modeling with a pretrained decoder-only LLM, using geometric tokens and learnable summary tokens to predict all part poses in a single pass with improved scalability and accuracy.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small 3D part assembly aims to reconstruct a complete shape from a set of unassembled parts by predicting a rigid SE(3) transformation for each part. Because the placement of a part is rarely determined by its own geometry, the task demands reasoning over the entire part set, and existing methods, which rely on pairwise relations or iterative generation and verification, scale poorly to objects with many parts. We present LLM2R, which casts part assembly as sequence modeling with a pretrained decoder-only large language model (LLM): a Point-BERT encoder and a Q-Former compress each part into a block of geometric tokens, the blocks of all parts are concatenated, and a causal LLM adapted with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) processes the sequence in one forward pass. Causal attention, however, lets the hidden states of a part observe only the parts that precede it. LLM2R therefore appends a block of learnable summary tokens after the last part: these tokens follow every part, so their states aggregate the whole assembly at a constant token cost, and a part-aware pose head fuses each part's states with them before predicting its rotation and translation. One architecture thus handles semantic and geometric assembly and predicts all poses in a single non-autoregressive pass. LLM2R achieves the highest part accuracy and success rate on all three PartNet categories, the best rotation error, translation error, and part accuracy on PartNeXt, and the lowest translation error and fastest inference on Breaking Bad, where only a fracture-specialized method is more accurate. Its advantage grows with the number of parts: at 100 parts it exceeds GARF by 33.5 points in part accuracy on Breaking Bad and Assembler by 29.1 points on PartNet, and it transfers zero-shot to unseen categories with more than 16 points higher part accuracy than the strongest of three baselines.

ru.title: Собираем любую 3D-конструкцию одним проходом LLM
ru.desc: Статья представляет LLM2R — метод сборки 3D-деталей, который рассматривает задачу как моделирование последовательностей с помощью предобученной decoder-only LLM. Каждая деталь кодируется в блок геометрических токенов через Point-BERT и Q-Former, а LLM с LoRA обрабатывает всю последовательность за один проход. Для учёта контекста всей сборки добавляются обучаемые суммирующие токены, которые агрегируют информацию о всех деталях, а голова предсказания поз вычисляет вращение и перенос каждой детали. Метод показывает лучшие результаты на наборах PartNet, PartNeXt и Breaking Bad, а его преимущество растёт с числом деталей.

en.title: Revolutionizing 3D Assembly with LLM2R: Fast, Accurate, and Scalable!
en.desc: LLM2R is a novel approach to 3D part assembly that utilizes a pretrained decoder-only large language model (LLM) to predict the poses of multiple parts in a single step. It transforms the assembly task into sequence modeling by encoding each part into geometric tokens and using learnable summary tokens to capture the overall context of the assembly. This method improves scalability and accuracy by allowing the model to reason over all parts simultaneously, rather than relying on pairwise comparisons or iterative methods. LLM2R outperforms existing techniques in accuracy and speed, especially as the number of parts increases, demonstrating significant advantages in complex assembly scenarios.

zh.title: LLM2R：高效的3D部件组装新方法
zh.desc: LLM2R将3D部件组装视为序列建模，利用预训练的解码器模型来提高可扩展性和准确性。该方法通过几何标记和可学习的摘要标记，在一次前向传递中预测所有部件的位置。与传统方法不同，LLM2R能够处理整个部件集的推理，避免了对成对关系或迭代生成的依赖。实验结果表明，LLM2R在多个数据集上表现出色，尤其是在部件准确性和推理速度方面。

papers.title: SpecKCast: Spectral Kalman Forecasting for Diffusion Acceleration
papers.abstract: Abstract SpecKCast forecasts diffusion transformer outputs in the frequency domain using per-band Kalman filters and adaptive step scheduling to accelerate inference with minimal memory overhead.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) achieve high-fidelity image and video generation, but they suffer from substantial inference costs due to repeated transformer evaluations across many denoising steps. Feature caching reduces this cost by reusing features across denoising steps. Recent forecasting methods extend this idea by extrapolating features to skipped steps instead of reusing them. However, existing forecasting methods extrapolate the features they predict uniformly, even though the spatial-frequency components of these features change most at different stages of denoising. They also overlook that denoising progresses nonuniformly, so equal step intervals can correspond to very different amounts of change. These mismatches amplify forecast errors as more steps are skipped, limiting the achievable acceleration. We propose SpecKCast, a training-free method that forecasts the model output in the frequency domain. SpecKCast applies a 2D discrete cosine transform (DCT) to the output and tracks each coefficient with a lightweight Kalman filter along a band-specific time coordinate derived from the noise schedule. The filter tracks each coefficient's value and rate of change, and the transformer is evaluated only when the filter's forecast uncertainty exceeds a threshold. Experiments on FLUX.1-dev, Qwen-Image, Wan2.1-14B, and HunyuanVideo show that SpecKCast achieves a better trade-off between acceleration and fidelity than existing caching and forecasting methods, reaching up to 6x speedup with less than 0.05 GiB of additional memory.

ru.title: Прогнозируй в частотах — и ускоряй диффузию без потери качества
ru.desc: Статья предлагает SpecKCast — метод ускорения инференса Diffusion Transformers без дообучения, который прогнозирует выход модели в частотной области. Выход преобразуется 2D DCT, а каждый коэффициент отслеживается легковесным фильтром Калмана по временной координате, привязанной к noise schedule. Трансформер вызывается только тогда, когда неопределённость прогноза превышает порог, что экономит вычисления на пропущенных шагах денойзинга. Эксперименты на FLUX.1-dev, Qwen-Image, Wan2.1-14B и HunyuanVideo показывают ускорение до 6x при минимальном росте памяти (менее 0.05 GiB) и лучшем балансе качества и скорости, чем у существующих методов кэширования и прогнозирования.

en.title: Accelerating Diffusion Transformers with Frequency Forecasting
en.desc: SpecKCast is a novel method that enhances the efficiency of diffusion transformers by forecasting their outputs in the frequency domain using Kalman filters. It addresses the high inference costs associated with repeated evaluations during denoising steps by intelligently predicting feature changes rather than reusing them uniformly. By applying a 2D discrete cosine transform (DCT) and tracking frequency coefficients, SpecKCast adapts to the nonuniform progression of denoising, allowing for significant acceleration without compromising output quality. The method demonstrates impressive results, achieving up to 6x speedup with minimal memory usage compared to traditional caching and forecasting techniques.

zh.title: SpecKCast：加速推理的新方法
zh.desc: SpecKCast是一种在频域中预测扩散变换器输出的方法，使用每个频段的卡尔曼滤波器和自适应步长调度来加速推理，同时保持较低的内存开销。该方法通过对输出应用二维离散余弦变换（DCT），并沿着特定时间坐标跟踪每个系数，来提高图像和视频生成的效率。与传统方法不同，SpecKCast考虑了去噪过程中的非均匀性，从而减少了预测误差。实验结果表明，SpecKCast在加速和保真度之间实现了更好的平衡，速度提升可达6倍，且额外内存使用少于0.05 GiB。

papers.title: Specter: Fast MoE Inference via Quantization-Enabled Multi-Step Speculative Offloading
papers.abstract: Abstract Specter accelerates single-GPU mixture-of-experts inference by combining quantized speculative decoding with expert offloading to hide PCIe latency and improve throughput.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Mixture-of-experts (MoE) models often exceed a single accelerator's memory capacity. Offloading experts to host memory creates a severe PCIe I/O bottleneck because data-dependent routing keeps transfers on the critical path. We present Specter, an inference system that uses quantization to combine speculative decoding with expert offloading. Its lightweight quantized draft model runs efficiently on device while preserving high-fidelity expert activation patterns. This provides accurate multi-step lookahead over future expert usage, allowing the runtime to organize expert movement and execution ahead of verification and improve both communication and execution efficiency. Under single-request inference, Specter achieves an average 1.50x (up to 1.88x) speedup in time per output token (TPOT) over the state-of-the-art system. Specter makes memory-constrained, single-GPU MoE inference more practical on commodity hardware. Our code is available at https://github.com/wwwwwf/specter_asplos.

ru.title: Быстрый MoE-инференс на одном GPU благодаря предсказанию экспертов
ru.desc: Статья представляет Specter — систему для инференса Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) моделей на одном GPU, когда веса экспертов не помещаются в память видеокарты. Главная идея — выгрузка экспертов в host-память и сокращение задержек PCIe за счёт квантованного speculative decoding, где лёгкая квантованная draft-модель заранее предсказывает будущие активации экспертов. Это позволяет заранее организовать перемещение и выполнение экспертов до верификации, пересекая передачу данных с вычислениями. В результате на одиночных запросах достигается в среднем 1.50x (до 1.88x) ускорение по TPOT относительно современных систем.

en.title: Accelerating MoE Inference with Specter: Speed and Efficiency Unleashed!
en.desc: Specter is a system designed to enhance the efficiency of single-GPU mixture-of-experts (MoE) inference by addressing memory limitations and latency issues. It utilizes quantized speculative decoding to predict expert usage, allowing for better organization of data transfers and execution. By offloading some expert computations to host memory, Specter minimizes the impact of PCIe bottlenecks, leading to improved throughput. The system demonstrates significant speed improvements, achieving up to 1.88 times faster inference times compared to existing methods, making it suitable for resource-constrained environments.

zh.title: Specter：提升单GPU混合专家推理的速度
zh.desc: Specter是一种加速单GPU混合专家推理的系统，它结合了量化的推测解码和专家卸载技术，以隐藏PCIe延迟并提高吞吐量。通过将专家卸载到主机内存，Specter解决了单个加速器内存容量不足的问题，同时避免了数据依赖路由造成的PCIe I/O瓶颈。该系统使用轻量级的量化草图模型，在设备上高效运行，并保持高保真度的专家激活模式。Specter在单请求推理中实现了平均1.50倍的速度提升，使得在普通硬件上进行内存受限的单GPU混合专家推理变得更加实用。

papers.title: Breaking Diffusion: Parallel Reasoning with Draft Refinement
papers.abstract: Abstract DRLMs refine draft answers via parallel token revisions and a single-pass cavity energy evaluation, outperforming autoregressive and diffusion baselines on reasoning tasks.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Drafting an answer allows a reasoning model to reconsider each decision in the context of the others. Yet repeated diffusion denoising does not ensure that individually plausible token updates form a better answer together. We introduce Draft Refinement Language Models (DRLMs), which use a single denoiser to propose parallel revisions and evaluate a candidate draft. We train the denoiser to reconstruct every token from uniformly corrupted drafts, teaching both preservation and repair. Its predictions specify revisions directly, without a diffusion reverse transition. Evaluation requires a different use of these predictions: confidence in an existing token reflects both contextual support and evidence from observing the token itself. Using the known corruption process, we correct for this self-token evidence to estimate how well each token is supported by the prompt and the remaining draft. Aggregating these estimates yields a cavity energy computed in one forward pass, without an additional scoring model. Each round proposes a revision, reads the completed candidate in its revised context, and retains it only if its energy is lower. Across Countdown, Sudoku-Extreme, and Maze-Hard, our method outperforms autoregressive and discrete diffusion baselines. With 6M parameters, DRLM reaches 44.4% on Countdown-5 and 93.9% on Sudoku-Extreme. The results establish complete-draft parallel refinement as an effective alternative to reverse diffusion for complex reasoning.

ru.title: Переписывать весь черновик целиком вместо пошагового шумоподавления
ru.desc: Статья представляет Draft Refinement Language Models (DRLM) — подход, в котором один денойзер параллельно предлагает правки всех токенов черновика ответа. Модель обучается восстанавливать токены из равномерно искажённых черновиков, без обратного перехода диффузии. Для оценки качества кандидата используется cavity energy, вычисляемая за один проход вперёд с поправкой на собственный вклад токена. Метод превосходит авторегрессионные и дискретные диффузионные модели на задачах Countdown, Sudoku-Extreme и Maze-Hard при всего 6M параметрах.

en.title: Parallel Refinement for Smarter Reasoning
en.desc: Draft Refinement Language Models (DRLMs) enhance the process of generating answers by allowing parallel token revisions and evaluating drafts in a single pass. Unlike traditional methods that rely on autoregressive or diffusion techniques, DRLMs utilize a denoiser to propose updates for multiple tokens simultaneously. This approach not only preserves the integrity of the draft but also repairs it by learning from corrupted versions of the text. The model's performance on reasoning tasks, such as Countdown and Sudoku, demonstrates its effectiveness in refining complex answers through a novel energy evaluation method.

zh.title: 草稿精炼：推理任务的新突破
zh.desc: 本文介绍了一种新的语言模型，称为草稿精炼语言模型（DRLMs），它通过并行的标记修订和单次的腔体能量评估来改进草稿答案。与自回归和扩散基线相比，DRLMs在推理任务上表现更优。该模型通过训练去重建每个标记，从而学习到保留和修复的能力，并在一次前向传递中计算腔体能量。实验结果表明，DRLMs在复杂推理任务中提供了一种有效的替代方案，超越了传统的反向扩散方法。

papers.title: EvaOmni: An Evidence-Grounded Benchmark for Audio-Visual Reasoning
papers.abstract: Abstract EvaOmni is an evidence-grounded benchmark that evaluates whether omnimodal language models identify audio-visual evidence and construct reasoning chains for audiovisual questions.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Omni LLMs can naturally locate key audio and visual evidence and integrate information across modalities for audiovisual reasoning. Existing audio-visual reasoning benchmarks that mainly rely on multiple-choice questions usually score models solely based on answer correctness, making it difficult to assess whether a model truly forms a reasoning chain from evidence to the correct answer. In addition, textual or unimodal shortcuts may allow models to answer correctly without analyzing the necessary audio-visual evidence, further weakening the reliability of evaluation benchmarks. To address these issues, we introduce EvaOmni, an evidence-grounded benchmark containing 392 videos and 1,027 purely human-annotated question-answer pairs, covering 15 capabilities and three levels: retrieval and localization, basic understanding, and complex reasoning. We design a series of rigorous annotation procedures in which experts annotate audio and visual evidence and construct video-based distractors; humans review whether questions meet strict inspection criteria, and finally models filter textual and unimodal shortcuts. Beyond high-quality question-answer pairs, we require models to simultaneously return the answer and supporting evidence intervals in order to evaluate the complete reasoning chain. We propose the Coverage Grounded Score (C.G.) to measure how much annotated evidence a model identifies, and the Bottleneck Grounded Score (B.G.) to penalize poor temporal localization in either modality; both are incorporated into answer correctness. Across 7 open-weight and 17 proprietary Omni LLMs, Gemini3.7-Flash achieved the highest overall accuracy (79.4%), C.G. (70.8%), and B.G. (35.1%). At Level 3, it reached 79.1% accuracy, but its B.G. was only 12.3%. These results show that even the most advanced models still have room for development in grounded audio-visual reasoning.
affiliations: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)

ru.title: Правильный ответ — не повод доверять модели: проверяем цепочку доказательств
ru.desc: Статья представляет EvaOmni — бенчмарк для оценки omnimodal LLM, который проверяет не только правильность ответа, но и умение находить аудио- и визуальные доказательства в видео и строить цепочку рассуждений. Датасет включает 392 видео и 1027 вопросов с ручной разметкой, дистракторами и фильтрацией текстовых и унимодальных шорткатов. Для оценки вводятся метрики Coverage Grounded Score (C.G.) и Bottleneck Grounded Score (B.G.), учитывающие полноту найденных доказательств и качество временной локализации. Результаты 24 моделей показывают, что даже лучшие системы, например Gemini3.7-Flash, плохо справляются с обоснованным audio-visual reasoning, несмотря на высокую точность ответов.

en.title: EvaOmni: Grounding Reasoning in Audio-Visual Evidence
en.desc: EvaOmni is a benchmark designed to evaluate how well omnimodal language models can identify and reason with audio-visual evidence for answering questions. Unlike traditional benchmarks that focus solely on answer correctness, EvaOmni emphasizes the importance of constructing reasoning chains from evidence to answers. It includes a diverse set of 392 videos and 1,027 human-annotated question-answer pairs, assessing models on their ability to retrieve, localize, and reason about audio-visual content. The introduction of Coverage Grounded Score (C.G.) and Bottleneck Grounded Score (B.G.) provides a more comprehensive evaluation of models' performance in grounded audio-visual reasoning.

zh.title: EvaOmni：音视频推理的新基准
zh.desc: EvaOmni是一个基于证据的基准，旨在评估全模态语言模型是否能够识别音频和视觉证据，并为音视频问题构建推理链。该基准包含392个视频和1,027个纯人类标注的问题-答案对，涵盖15种能力和三个层次。我们设计了一系列严格的标注程序，以确保模型不仅能正确回答问题，还能返回支持证据的时间区间，从而评估完整的推理链。通过引入覆盖基础分数和瓶颈基础分数，我们能够更全面地评估模型在音视频推理中的表现。

papers.title: Evolving Agent Interfaces
papers.abstract: Abstract Agent S4 autonomously evolves computer-use interfaces from task experience, significantly improving open-source agent performance and reducing costs compared to larger proprietary models.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Computer-use agents are limited by the interfaces humans give them. An agent may type a spreadsheet cell by cell when a single line of code would do, or print all two thousand lines of a file through a shell to find one function. Both the interfaces and the knowledge of when to use each are built by hand, which cannot keep pace with new applications, workflows, and models. We argue that interface design should itself be an agent capability. We introduce Agent S4, an autonomous computer-use scientist that builds Evolving Agent Interfaces from task experience. A meta-agent examines task agents' trajectories on synthetic training tasks, without success labels, and constructs and revises interfaces and usage knowledge in a repository. Population-based evolution then selects which repositories to develop further by their performance on validation tasks the meta-agent never sees, favoring changes that generalize beyond the seen tasks. On OSWorld V2, Agent S4, with Qwen3.8-27B and the evolved repository of interfaces, sets a new state of the art in open-source computer-use agents, reaching 21.3% binary score, 3.8 times the same model with fixed interfaces. This is above both GPT-5.5 (13.0%) and Claude Opus 4.8 (20.6%), at about 4.3% and 1.5% of their respective costs. On ScienceBoard, the evolved interfaces improve the success rate from 41.4% to 58.6% with the same model. These results suggest that useful interfaces can be evolved from experience, making autonomous interface design a source of improvement complementary to advances in models and harnesses. We open-source our code at https://github.com/simular-ai/agent-s.

ru.title: Агент сам эволюционирует интерфейсы и обгоняет гигантов
ru.desc: Авторы представляют Agent S4 — автономного агента для работы с компьютером, который сам проектирует интерфейсы взаимодействия на основе опыта решения задач. Мета-агент анализирует траектории работы агентов на синтетических задачах без меток успеха и формирует репозиторий интерфейсов и знаний об их использовании. Популяционная эволюция отбирает варианты по качеству на валидационных задачах, которые мета-агент не видит, что способствует обобщению. На бенчмарках OSWorld V2 и ScienceBoard открытая модель Qwen с эволюционировавшими интерфейсами превосходит GPT-5.5 и Claude Opus 4.8 при значительно меньшей стоимости.

en.title: Evolving Interfaces for Smarter Agents
en.desc: Agent S4 is a novel machine learning framework that autonomously evolves computer-use interfaces based on task experience, enhancing the performance of open-source agents. It utilizes a meta-agent to analyze the trajectories of task agents on synthetic tasks, allowing it to create and refine interfaces without needing success labels. By employing population-based evolution, Agent S4 selects the most effective interface designs based on their performance on unseen validation tasks. This approach not only improves efficiency but also significantly reduces costs compared to larger proprietary models, demonstrating that adaptive interface design can lead to substantial advancements in agent capabilities.

zh.title: 自主进化接口，提升智能体性能！
zh.desc: 本文介绍了Agent S4，这是一种自主进化计算机使用接口的智能体，能够通过任务经验显著提升开源智能体的性能并降低成本。传统的计算机使用智能体受限于人类设计的接口，导致效率低下，而Agent S4通过构建和修订接口知识库，自动优化这些接口。该智能体利用元智能体分析任务智能体在合成训练任务中的轨迹，选择性能优异的接口进行进一步开发。实验结果表明，Agent S4在多个任务上超越了现有的先进模型，证明了自主接口设计的潜力。

papers.title: Painting Change Map as guidance for generating painting processes
papers.abstract: Abstract This work introduces a spatio-temporal Painting Change Map to control video generation of artwork by tracking localized structural changes across time, enabling fine-grained guidance for painting and unpainting processes.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Digital art generation has undergone a massive paradigm shift, moving from static image synthesis to dynamic video generation that can mimic the human painting process. While existing models can synthesize visually stunning time-lapses of paintings being created or "unpainted," they largely treat the creative process as a black box. Current conditioning mechanisms are either too rigid, relying on static geometric cues like Canny edges or depth maps, or too holistic, utilizing simple scalar progress variables that offer no localized control. Consequently, users lack the agency to steer how a painting evolves over time. In this work, we argue that true control over the video generation of artwork requires a joint understanding of two fundamental dimensions: where an artist acts, and when those actions take place. To achieve this, we introduce the Painting Change Map, a novel spatio-temporal control mechanism that explicitly tracks normalized structural changes across a 1,000-timestep continuum, a resolution sufficient to capture fine-grained stroke-level changes while remaining computationally tractable. By mapping localized visual differences into an encoded RGB space, our representation enables fine-grained guidance for both the forward painting and reverse unpainting processes. Extensive benchmarking demonstrates the efficacy of our approach. We outperform existing control baselines and achieve competitive or superior results compared to state-of-the-art painting methods. Furthermore, under oracle conditions, our method surpasses all baselines by a significant margin. Code is available at https://github.com/Markus-Pobitzer/painting-change-map.

ru.title: Управляй не только где, но и когда художник делает мазок
ru.desc: Авторы представляют Painting Change Map — пространственно-временной механизм управления для генерации видео картин, который отслеживает локальные структурные изменения на шкале из 1000 временных шагов. Карта изменений кодируется в RGB-пространство и подаётся как условие для модели генерации, что позволяет точно задавать процессы рисования и «стирания» картины по мелким мазкам. Такой подход превосходит существующие методы управления, основанные на Canny-границах, картах глубины или скалярном прогрессе, которые дают лишь грубый контроль. По результатам бенчмарков метод сравним или превосходит современные решения для генерации процесса живописи, а в условиях oracle-оценки значительно опережает все baseline-модели.

en.title: Mastering Art Evolution: Fine-Grained Control in Video Generation
en.desc: This paper presents a new method called the Painting Change Map, which allows for detailed control over video generation of artwork by tracking changes in painting over time. Unlike previous models that treat the painting process as a black box, this approach provides localized guidance on where and when changes occur in the artwork. By encoding visual differences into an RGB space, it enables precise manipulation of both painting and unpainting processes. The results show that this method outperforms existing techniques, offering superior control and quality in dynamic art generation.

zh.title: 掌控艺术创作的时空变化
zh.desc: 本文提出了一种时空绘画变化图，用于控制艺术作品的视频生成，通过跟踪时间上的局部结构变化，实现对绘画和撤销过程的精细指导。随着数字艺术生成的快速发展，从静态图像合成转向动态视频生成，现有模型在创作过程中往往将其视为黑箱。当前的条件机制要么过于僵化，依赖静态几何线索，要么过于整体，缺乏局部控制。我们的研究表明，真正控制艺术作品视频生成需要理解艺术家的行为发生的地点和时间，并通过绘画变化图实现这一目标。

papers.title: PhysSkin++: Real-Time and Generalizable Physics-Based Animation via Self-Supervised Neural Skinning
papers.abstract: Abstract PhysSkin++ learns continuous neural skinning fields from static shapes to enable real-time, physics-based animation across diverse geometries and spatial representations without per-object training.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Generalizing real-time physics-based animation across diverse 3D shapes and spatial discretizations remains challenging. In this paper, we introduce PhysSkin++, a physics-informed framework that learns continuous neural skinning fields from static geometries to construct compact deformation subspaces. Specifically, we propose a Neural Skinning Fields Autoencoder that predicts shape-dependent deformation subspaces without per-object network training. To learn these subspaces without simulation trajectories, we develop a Physics-Informed Self-Supervised Learning strategy that combines skinning-field normalization with conflict-aware gradient correction, stabilizing joint optimization under physical and orthogonality constraints. The learned representation supports efficient reduced dynamics with user control and contact interactions, together with direct animation binding to meshes, point clouds, and 3D Gaussians. For prescribed rig animation, we further introduce a self-supervised complementarity objective to learn complementary elastic responses without enforcing complementarity constraints at runtime. Experiments demonstrate cross-shape generalization of the learned skinning fields, real-time reduced simulation, and applications to controllable, collision-aware, and rig-complementary animation.

ru.title: Физическая анимация любых 3D-форм в реальном времени без переобучения
ru.desc: PhysSkin++ — это фреймворк, который обучает непрерывные нейронные поля скиннинга (neural skinning fields) по статическим 3D-формам без симуляционных траекторий. Autoencoder предсказывает компактные подпространства деформаций, зависящие от формы, без дообучения сети под каждый объект. Self-supervised обучение с физическими ограничениями, нормализацией полей и conflict-aware коррекцией градиентов стабилизирует оптимизацию. Это позволяет проводить real-time reduced-симуляцию с управлением, учётом контактов и привязкой анимации к мешам, облакам точек и 3D Gaussians.

en.title: Real-Time Physics-Based Animation for Diverse 3D Shapes
en.desc: PhysSkin++ is a novel framework that learns continuous neural skinning fields from static shapes, allowing for real-time physics-based animation across various 3D geometries without needing to train separate models for each object. It utilizes a Neural Skinning Fields Autoencoder to predict deformation subspaces that are specific to different shapes, streamlining the animation process.
