The framework employs a Physics-Informed Self-Supervised Learning approach, which stabilizes the optimization process by integrating physical constraints and gradient corrections. This results in efficient dynamics that can handle user interactions and complex animations, demonstrating the ability to generalize across different shapes and support real-time applications.

zh.title: 实时物理动画的新突破
zh.desc: PhysSkin++ 是一个学习连续神经皮肤场的框架，能够从静态形状中实现实时的基于物理的动画。它通过构建紧凑的变形子空间，避免了对每个对象进行单独训练。该方法结合了皮肤场归一化和冲突感知梯度修正，确保在物理和正交约束下的稳定优化。实验结果表明，PhysSkin++ 能够实现跨形状的泛化，支持可控的、碰撞感知的动画。

papers.title: Epi: Towards a Persistent, Self-Improving Agent for Autonomous Research
papers.abstract: Abstract Épi is an autonomous research agent that maintains persistent investigations across sessions, improves through accumulated experience, and achieves record-setting mathematical and algorithmic results with reduced computational cost.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small We present Épi, an autonomous research agent that sustains investigations across model sessions and evolves its methods through accumulated experience. Épi combines persistent research history, hierarchical memory, branching and independent review to maintain research continuity, learn from experiments, and explore and revisit alternative approaches. Its experiments run across session boundaries, and a fixed verifier evaluates their outputs. Épi produced 120 record-setting results, comprising 20 numerical bound records across 12 families and 100 construction records across eight families. These include an approximately 84-fold narrower interval for the n-queens constant and a more than 3.6-million-fold narrower rigorous interval for the quartic Feigenbaum attractor dimension. Exact dual certificates establish that the Cohn-Elkies linear-programming bound cannot be sharp in dimensions 10 and 11. Beyond numerical improvements, Épi gives a computer-assisted proof of Tuza's conjecture for split graphs with an eight-vertex clique part and at most three triangle-active neighborhood types, with arbitrary multiplicities. We extend this research process to algorithmic coding with Épi-turbo, a lightweight configuration that develops executable solvers for tasks including vehicle routing, scheduling and production planning. On 30 FrontierOR tasks, Épi-turbo achieves a 5.4% higher total benchmark score than Codex at 64% of its model cost, using the same underlying model and reasoning effort. Épi is designed to support human understanding by connecting computational results to explicit methods and mathematical arguments that researchers can examine and build upon.

ru.title: Автономный ИИ-исследователь, который учится на собственном опыте
ru.desc: Статья представляет Épi — автономного исследовательского агента, который ведёт долгосрочные исследования между сессиями модели и улучшает свои методы на основе накопленного опыта. Агент использует историю исследований, иерархическую память, ветвление и независимую проверку, а результаты его экспериментов оцениваются фиксированным верификатором. Épi получил 120 рекордных результатов в математике и алгоритмах, включая доказательство гипотезы Tuza для определённого класса split-графов. Также вариант Épi-turbo на 30 задачах FrontierOR набрал на 5.4% больше баллов, чем Codex, при стоимости модели 64% от его стоимости.

en.title: Épi: Revolutionizing Autonomous Research with Continuous Learning and Record-Setting Results
en.desc: Épi is an autonomous research agent that enhances its performance by learning from past experiences and maintaining continuity in its investigations across different sessions. It utilizes advanced techniques like hierarchical memory and independent review to explore various research paths and improve its methods. Épi has achieved significant mathematical breakthroughs, including record-setting results in numerical bounds and algorithmic proofs, while also reducing computational costs. Additionally, its lightweight version, Épi-turbo, excels in developing efficient solvers for complex tasks, outperforming existing models in benchmark tests.

zh.title: 自主研究代理Épi：持续学习与创新的结合
zh.desc: Épi是一个自主研究代理，能够在多个会话中持续进行研究，并通过积累的经验不断改进其方法。它结合了持久的研究历史、分层记忆和独立审查，以保持研究的连续性，学习实验结果，并探索不同的方法。Épi在多个领域取得了120项创纪录的成果，包括数值界限和构造记录，显著提高了计算效率。它还通过Épi-turbo扩展了算法编码，能够为车辆调度、排程和生产规划等任务开发可执行的求解器。

papers.title: FlowState: Execution State as Memory for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Abstract FlowState improves long-horizon agent performance by maintaining structured, revisitable execution memory with incremental updates and progressive access, reducing token use while increasing success rates.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Long-horizon tasks require LLM agents to continually draw on information from earlier interactions. However, retaining the full history increases context costs, while compressing it risks losing details needed later, and the relevance of historical information often becomes apparent as the task progresses. To address these challenges, we propose FlowState, which treats execution state as memory that can be retained and revisited across requests, unifying current decision-making with the reuse of historical information. FlowState preserves semantically typed state nodes, their relations, and references to raw tool observations, separating persistent retention from on-demand access. Within a single execution loop, Incremental State Update (ISU) maintains the current state based on new inputs and feedback, while Progressive State Access (PSA) progressively reveals historical states and supporting evidence as needed during reasoning. Together, these mechanisms enable agents to reassess prior decisions in light of new information and guide subsequent actions. Compared with a full-context baseline using the same DeepSeek-V4-Flash model, FlowState improves the average success rate on MemoryArena and the average pass rate on τ^3-Bench by 4.55 and 13.95 percentage points, respectively, while reducing total token consumption by 43.2% and 40.6%. These results demonstrate the performance and efficiency advantages of FlowState on long-horizon tasks.

ru.title: Память агента, которая помнит нужное и тратит меньше токенов
ru.desc: В статье предлагается FlowState — подход к памяти LLM-агентов для долгих задач, где состояние выполнения хранится как структурированный граф типизированных узлов со связями и ссылками на сырые результаты инструментов. Механизм Incremental State Update (ISU) инкрементально обновляет текущее состояние на основе новых входных данных и обратной связи, а Progressive State Access (PSA) постепенно раскрывает историческую информацию по мере необходимости. Такой подход позволяет агенту пересматривать прошлые решения, сохраняя при этом важные детали, которые могли бы потеряться при сжатии контекста. В экспериментах с моделью DeepSeek-V4-Flash FlowState повысил успешность на MemoryArena и τ³-Bench и одновременно сократил потребление токенов примерно на 40%.

en.title: FlowState: Enhancing Long-Horizon Task Performance with Smart Memory Management
en.desc: FlowState is a novel approach designed to enhance the performance of agents in long-horizon tasks by effectively managing execution memory. It allows agents to maintain a structured memory that can be revisited, which helps in reducing the number of tokens used while improving success rates. The method incorporates Incremental State Update (ISU) to adjust the current state based on new inputs and Progressive State Access (PSA) to gradually reveal relevant historical information as needed. This combination enables agents to make better decisions by reassessing past actions with the latest context, leading to significant improvements in task performance and efficiency.

zh.title: FlowState：提升长时间任务智能体表现的记忆机制
zh.desc: FlowState是一种改进长时间任务表现的机制，通过维护结构化的可重访执行记忆来实现。它允许智能体在执行过程中逐步更新和访问历史信息，从而减少了令牌的使用，同时提高了成功率。FlowState将执行状态视为可以在请求之间保留和重访的记忆，统一了当前决策与历史信息的重用。通过增量状态更新和渐进状态访问，FlowState使智能体能够根据新信息重新评估先前的决策，并指导后续行动。

papers.title: Event-STVG: Spatio-Temporal Video Grounding for Long-Form Event Reasoning
papers.abstract: Abstract Event-STVG introduces a challenging benchmark requiring multimodal models to perform long-form event reasoning, repeated-event disambiguation, and multi-target spatio-temporal grounding across extended video contexts.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Spatio-Temporal Video Grounding (STVG) aims to jointly localize a target in space and time given a natural-language query. Despite continued advances, existing STVG benchmarks remain largely centered on localizing targets through instance-specific descriptions, leaving them largely decoupled from long-form reasoning increasingly emphasized in multimodal large language models (MLLMs). In this paper, we introduce Event-STVG, a task that shifts STVG from locating what is described toward event-level reasoning by unifying long-form context, repeated-event reasoning, event localization, role inference, and multi-target grounding. To facilitate research on Event-STVG, we construct a large-scale benchmark comprising 4,016 annotated event occurrences across soccer and seven additional domains. Experiments with state-of-the-art MLLMs reveal substantial difficulty, with the strongest model achieving only 5.4% m-vIoU at the 10-minute horizon. Across domains, we consistently observe confusion among repeated same-type events, spatial grounding bottlenecks, and rare success in jointly grounding all required roles. Event-STVG establishes a new challenge for visual understanding in MLLMs, calling for future models that can jointly reason about complex events across space and time. Code and annotations are available at https://github.com/THU-KEG/EventSTVG
affiliations: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

ru.title: От поиска объектов к пониманию событий во времени и пространстве
ru.desc: В статье представлен Event-STVG — новая задача пространственно-временной локализации видео по текстовому запросу, которая смещает фокус с поиска конкретного объекта на рассуждения о событиях. Авторы объединяют длинный видеоконтекст, различение повторяющихся событий, определение ролей участников и многоцелевую локализацию. Для исследований создан крупный бенчмарк из 4016 размеченных событий в футболе и семи других доменах. Эксперименты показывают, что даже лучшие мультимодальные LLM справляются с задачей очень плохо: наилучший результат составляет лишь 5.4% m-vIoU на горизонте 10 минут.

en.title: Revolutionizing Event Reasoning in Video Understanding
en.desc: Event-STVG is a new benchmark that tests multimodal models on complex tasks involving long-form event reasoning and spatio-temporal grounding in videos. It focuses on understanding events in a broader context rather than just identifying specific instances, which is a limitation of current benchmarks. The paper presents a large-scale dataset with over 4,000 annotated events across various domains, highlighting the challenges models face in accurately localizing and reasoning about repeated events. The findings indicate that existing models struggle significantly, achieving low performance, which underscores the need for advancements in visual understanding for multimodal large language models.

zh.title: Event-STVG：多模态事件推理的新挑战
zh.desc: Event-STVG是一个新的基准测试，要求多模态模型在扩展视频上下文中进行长形式事件推理、重复事件消歧和多目标时空定位。该任务将STVG从简单的目标定位转向事件级推理，结合了长形式上下文、重复事件推理、事件定位、角色推断和多目标定位。我们构建了一个包含4016个注释事件的规模庞大的基准，涵盖足球和其他七个领域。实验结果显示，现有的多模态大语言模型在这一任务上面临重大挑战，呼吁未来的模型能够更好地理解复杂事件。

papers.title: DecisionPivot: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Decision Models in LLM Systems
papers.abstract: Abstract DecisionPivot is a diagnostic benchmark that evaluates decision models across controlled variations, revealing gaps between aggregate accuracy, contrast-group performance, calibration, and reasoning effort.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Decision models support routing, guardrails, and output verification in LLM systems. However, item accuracy alone cannot establish whether models make correct decisions across controlled variations or assign reliable confidence to their predictions. We introduce DecisionPivot, a diagnostic benchmark comprising 48 tasks and 40,033 items across seven decision roles. Its core track contains 7,800 items from 13 generated task families, organized into contrast groups with computed answers verified by independently implemented solvers. The complementary reference track contains 32,233 items from 35 public test sets, preserving their original evaluation metrics. We evaluate 40 decision models and 14 general models using documented, model-specific protocols, assessing item and contrast-group accuracy, probability ordering, calibration, and empirical selective coverage. Our results reveal substantial differences obscured by aggregate scores: two 27B models separated by only 2.6 points on the reference track achieve contrast-group accuracies of 70.1% and 44.2%. Across 2,400 binary contrast pairs, Perplexity Decider correctly ranks the positive member above the negative member in 92.3% of pairs but answers both members correctly in only 74.1%, exposing a gap between probability ordering and decision correctness. Models with similar item accuracy also differ in the reliability of their high-confidence predictions. On a separate 1,296-item subset, GLM-5.3 achieves 93.5\% contrast-group accuracy at a higher reasoning setting, compared with 81.5% at its lowest effort. By linking errors to pivotal details and difficulty levels, DecisionPivot provides fine-grained diagnostics of decision failures that aggregate evaluation alone cannot reveal.

ru.title: Высокая точность не означает правильного решения: диагностика decision-моделей
ru.desc: Статья представляет DecisionPivot — диагностический бенчмарк для оценки decision-моделей, которые используются для маршрутизации, guardrails и верификации выходов в LLM-системах. Основной трек содержит 7 800 элементов из 13 сгенерированных семейств задач, сгруппированных в контрастные группы, а справочный трек включает 32 233 элемента из 35 публичных тестовых наборов. Оценка 40 decision-моделей и 14 общих моделей показывает, что агрегированная accuracy скрывает важные различия в contrast-group accuracy, ранжировании вероятностей, calibration и selective coverage. Результаты демонстрируют, что высокая точность на отдельных элементах не гарантирует корректных решений на контрастных парах и надежной уверенности, а также что reasoning effort существенно влияет на качество.

en.title: Uncovering Hidden Gaps in Decision Model Performance
en.desc: DecisionPivot is a benchmark designed to assess decision models by examining their performance across various controlled scenarios. It highlights the importance of not just overall accuracy but also the reliability of predictions and the reasoning effort involved in decision-making. The benchmark includes a comprehensive set of tasks and items, allowing for detailed analysis of how different models perform under specific conditions. By revealing discrepancies in model performance that aggregate scores may hide, DecisionPivot helps identify areas for improvement in decision-making systems.

zh.title: 揭示决策模型的真实表现
zh.desc: DecisionPivot 是一个诊断基准，用于评估决策模型在控制变量下的表现，揭示聚合准确性、对比组性能、校准和推理努力之间的差距。该基准包含 48 个任务和 40,033 个项目，涵盖七种决策角色，帮助分析模型在不同情况下的决策能力。通过对 40 个决策模型和 14 个通用模型的评估，发现即使在聚合分数相近的情况下，模型的决策准确性和高置信度预测的可靠性也存在显著差异。DecisionPivot 通过将错误与关键细节和难度水平关联，提供了细致的决策失败诊断，超越了单一的聚合评估。

papers.title: From Short Clips to Real-Time Streams: Identity-Aware Supervision and Context-Efficient Generation for Video Face Swapping
papers.abstract: Abstract StreamingSwap is a real-time flow-matching framework for video face swapping that improves identity fidelity and efficiency via joint identity-reconstruction loss and reduced spatial-temporal generation, achieving stable 20 FPS performance on long videos.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Video face swapping transfers the reference identity to a target video while preserving its other attributes and motion. Despite recent progress in reference-guided flow-based methods, jointly achieving faithful identity transfer, high fidelity, and real-time generation over long video streams remains challenging. To address this challenge, we rethink the task-specific structure of reference-guided video face swapping. First, face swapping changes only identity while preserving most visual content, yet flow-matching supervision is weakly sensitive to these changes. We therefore develop Joint Rec-ID Loss, which balances explicit identity supervision and latent reconstruction according to the noise level. Second, the target video already provides non-edited attributes and temporal dynamics, enabling generation with fewer spatial tokens and shorter temporal contexts through Face-RoI Generation and Short-Context Rollout Training. By integrating these designs, we propose StreamingSwap, a reference-guided flow-matching framework for real-time streaming video face swapping. We also introduce HumanFaceVid, comprising 1,000 hours of cinematic training data and evaluation sets of 200 short and 200 long videos. Experiments demonstrate that our method achieves competitive identity transfer and visual quality at 20 FPS on a single NVIDIA RTX 4090 GPU, with stable generation over videos up to 10 minutes long. Project webpage: https://aim-uofa.github.io/StreamingSwap/

ru.title: Замена лица в видео в реальном времени без потери идентичности
ru.desc: Статья представляет StreamingSwap — фреймворк на основе flow-matching для замены лиц в видео в реальном времени с сохранением идентичности. Ключевые идеи: Joint Rec-ID Loss, который балансирует explicit identity supervision и latent reconstruction в зависимости от уровня шума, и генерация только по области лица (Face-RoI Generation) с короткими временными контекстами (Short-Context Rollout Training). Авторы также представляют датасет HumanFaceVid с 1000 часами кинематографических данных и тестовыми наборами видео. Модель работает со скоростью 20 FPS на одной NVIDIA RTX 4090 и стабильна на видео до 10 минут.

en.title: Real-Time Face Swapping with StreamingSwap
en.desc: StreamingSwap is a novel framework designed for real-time video face swapping that enhances identity accuracy and processing speed. It utilizes a Joint Rec-ID Loss to effectively balance identity supervision and reconstruction, allowing for better fidelity in identity transfer. The framework also incorporates Face-RoI Generation and Short-Context Rollout Training to optimize the use of spatial and temporal data, enabling efficient processing of long video streams. With its ability to maintain 20 FPS performance on lengthy videos, StreamingSwap represents a significant advancement in reference-guided flow-based methods for face swapping.

zh.title: 实时视频换脸的新突破
zh.desc: StreamingSwap 是一个实时流匹配框架，用于视频换脸，旨在通过联合身份重建损失和减少时空生成来提高身份保真度和效率。该方法能够在长视频上实现稳定的每秒20帧性能，同时保持目标视频的其他属性和运动。我们提出的联合重建身份损失能够平衡显式身份监督和潜在重建，从而增强对身份变化的敏感性。此外，通过人脸区域生成和短时上下文训练，减少了所需的空间标记和时间上下文，使得生成过程更加高效。

papers.title: EdgeKernelBench: Unified LLM-Driven Kernel Generation for Edge Backends
papers.abstract: Abstract EdgeKernelBench and LEKA enable unified evaluation and layered optimization of LLM-generated kernels across heterogeneous edge backends, revealing a gap between correctness and performance.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Recent works show that LLMs can generate kernels with strong performance on server GPUs. Edge deployment presents distinct challenges because the hardware is heterogeneous, the software stacks are fragmented, and the resource budgets are tight. LLM kernel generation across diverse edge backends has yet to be studied systematically. We introduce EdgeKernelBench, which combines a unified IR deployment framework with a hierarchical benchmark for edge workloads. The unified IR captures reusable computation, scheduling, and memory decisions and connects to each target backend through a compiler interface. The benchmark spans progressively larger program scopes, from individual operators to compact model graphs, across representative edge application domains. We instantiate the design with TVM as a reference compiler and validate it across heterogeneous edge backends. With a single generation attempt, the best model achieves 64.5% Correct@1 but only 25.5% Fast@1.0. This gap shows that functional correctness does not consistently translate into performance gains. We therefore introduce the Layered Edge Kernel Agent (LEKA), which organizes optimization through a layered IR. On the agent evaluation subset, LEKA achieves 43.5% Fast@1.0, compared with 13.0% for direct generation and 26.1% for Claude Code. LEKA and Claude Code use the same base model and optimization budget. Together, EdgeKernelBench and LEKA support unified evaluation and layered optimization of kernels generated by LLMs across edge backends.

ru.title: Корректный код — это ещё не быстрый код: слоистая оптимизация ядер LLM для edge-устройств
ru.desc: Статья представляет EdgeKernelBench — единый фреймворк и иерархический бенчмарк для оценки ядер (kernels), которые генерируют LLM для разнородных edge-устройств с фрагментированным ПО и ограниченными ресурсами. В основе лежит унифицированное промежуточное представление (IR), которое через компилятор TVM связывает вычисления, планирование и управление памятью с разными аппаратными бэкендами. Эксперименты показывают разрыв между корректностью (Correct@1 = 64.5%) и производительностью (Fast@1.0 = 25.5%) сгенерированных ядер. Для его преодоления авторы предлагают LEKA — послойного агента оптимизации, который достигает 43.5% Fast@1.0 против 13.0% при прямой генерации и 26.1% у Claude Code.

en.title: Bridging the Gap: Optimizing LLM Kernels for Edge Performance
en.desc: This paper presents EdgeKernelBench and LEKA, tools designed to evaluate and optimize kernels generated by large language models (LLMs) for edge computing environments. The research highlights the challenges of deploying LLM-generated kernels on heterogeneous hardware, where performance and correctness can diverge significantly. EdgeKernelBench provides a unified intermediate representation (IR) framework that facilitates benchmarking across various edge workloads, while LEKA introduces a layered approach to optimize these kernels. The findings reveal that while LLMs can generate functionally correct kernels, achieving high performance remains a challenge, underscoring the need for systematic evaluation and optimization strategies.

zh.title: 统一评估与分层优化：提升边缘内核性能的关键
zh.desc: EdgeKernelBench和LEKA提供了对LLM生成的内核在异构边缘后端的统一评估和分层优化。这项研究揭示了正确性与性能之间的差距，尤其是在边缘部署中，由于硬件异构、软件堆栈分散和资源预算紧张，面临独特挑战。EdgeKernelBench结合了统一的中间表示（IR）部署框架和分层基准测试，能够捕捉可重用的计算、调度和内存决策。LEKA通过分层IR组织优化，显著提高了性能，展示了在边缘应用领域中优化LLM生成内核的潜力。

papers.title: Good Judgment, Bad Advice: Decision-Model Controllers Raise Agent Cost Without Improving Success
papers.abstract: Abstract A typed decision model consulted at fixed points increased agent costs without improving success rates, despite better ranking of finish requests, due to poor calibration.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Agent scaffolds increasingly delegate small decisions (whether to stop, verify, or change approach) to cheaper models. We ask whether a typed decision model, Jev 1.13, consulted only at deterministic decision points, makes a Claude Sonnet 5.5 terminal agent cheaper without making it worse. In a pre-specified study on Terminal-Bench 2.1, we hold one agent loop fixed and vary only the controller: none, deterministic rules, a small LLM (Claude Haiku 5.5) answering the same questions, Jev, and a placebo that samples Jev's development-phase choice frequencies at the same moments. On 21 held-out tasks (315 trials), Jev raised cost per attempt by 19% (geometric-mean ratio 1.19, 95% CI 1.02-1.36) at an identical pass rate (73.0% vs. 73.0%). Jev was cheaper than the small-LLM controller (ratio 0.81) but 22% more expensive than the placebo, and no pass-rate difference between arms was detectable. Offline, Jev ranked finish requests better than the alternatives (AUROC 0.78 vs. 0.62 for rules and 0.60 for the small LLM) but was poorly calibrated: its mean probability that a run was complete was 0.50 when 87% of those runs passed, so it asked the agent to verify work that was already correct. No controller ever chose to abandon a run. Informative decision signals did not become useful interventions; we discuss what that would require.

ru.title: Хороший ранжир без калибровки не экономит деньги агента
ru.desc: В статье исследуется, можно ли удешевить агента для терминальных задач (Claude Sonnet 5.5), делегируя мелкие решения, например, остановиться ли, проверить ли результат или сменить подход, типизированной модели Jev 1.13. На Terminal-Bench 2.1 сравнивались пять контроллеров, включая правила, маленькую LLM и плацебо, при фиксированном цикле агента. Jev лучше ранжировал запросы на завершение (AUROC 0.78), но был плохо откалиброван, поэтому стоимость выросла на 19% без улучшения доли успешных прогонов. Авторы делают вывод, что информативные сигналы решений не превращаются в полезные вмешательства без корректной калибровки вероятностей.

en.title: Balancing Cost and Performance in Decision Models
en.desc: This paper investigates the effectiveness of a typed decision model, Jev 1.13, in improving the performance of a terminal agent while managing costs. The study reveals that although Jev improved the ranking of finish requests, it increased the cost per attempt by 19% without enhancing the success rate. The results indicate that Jev was more cost-effective than a small language model but less so than a placebo, highlighting issues with its calibration. Ultimately, the findings suggest that better decision signals are needed to translate into meaningful improvements in agent performance.

zh.title: 类型化决策模型的成本与效果分析
zh.desc: 这篇论文探讨了一种类型化决策模型（Jev 1.13）在固定决策点的应用，发现其增加了代理的成本，但并未提高成功率。尽管Jev在完成请求的排名上表现更好，但由于校准不佳，导致其在实际应用中效果不理想。研究表明，Jev的使用使得每次尝试的成本提高了19%，而且与其他控制器相比，其通过率没有显著差异。论文还讨论了如何使信息决策信号转变为有效的干预措施。

papers.title: Unsupervised Tool Evolution for Coding Agents in Data-Lake Analytics
papers.abstract: Abstract TEAL evolves reusable data-analysis tools for coding agents without ground-truth labels by combining data-driven exploration and trajectory-based critique, improving accuracy under tight step budgets.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Coding agents can answer analytical questions over a data lake by discovering, cleaning, and joining the relevant data. However, they discard this work after each question and redo it from scratch for the next one. Tool evolution, which automatically builds and refines reusable tools across tasks, is a natural fit for this repetition. Since a ground-truth label for a data-lake question requires an expert to solve it first, we consider the unsupervised setting. We propose TEAL (Tool Evolution for Analytics over data Lakes), which evolves a library of tools and usage skills for a given Worker agent without labels. Two agents propose tools from complementary evidence, an Explorer from the data lake itself and a Critic from Worker trajectories. A proposed change is kept only if the Worker adopts the tool on a rerun without extra steps and any changed answer is supported by trajectory evidence. We also introduce TEAL-Q, which generates synthetic questions for tool evolution when real ones are unavailable. We evaluate on KramaBench and LakeQA with four Worker LLMs under step budgets, which cap the number of steps the Worker may take per question. With a tight budget of 10 or 15 steps, TEAL improves every Worker on both benchmarks, lifting Sonnet-5 at 15 steps by 9.3 points on KramaBench and 21.7 points on LakeQA. A tighter budget also yields better feedback for evolution. For example, Sonnet-5's LakeQA library evolved at 20 steps and deployed unchanged at 30 steps scores 68.3, above both the baseline (59.6) and a library evolved directly at 30 steps (64.2). Additionally, a library evolved on synthetic questions performs comparably to one evolved on real questions. These results show that useful tools can be evolved without labels, and hopefully inspire future work on what to evolve and how to obtain feedback in unsupervised agent evolution.

ru.title: Инструменты для AI-агентов, которые учатся без разметки
ru.desc: Статья представляет TEAL, метод эволюции набора переиспользуемых инструментов для coding agents, которые отвечают на аналитические вопросы по data lake. Метод работает без размеченных данных: агент-Explorer предлагает инструменты на основе самих данных, а агент-Critic анализирует траектории работы Worker LLM. Изменение сохраняется, только если Worker использует инструмент без дополнительных шагов и ответы подтверждаются траекториями. Эксперименты на KramaBench и LakeQA показывают заметный рост точности при жёстком бюджете шагов, а синтетические вопросы (TEAL-Q) дают результаты, сравнимые с реальными.

en.title: Evolving Data-Analysis Tools Without Labels
en.desc: TEAL (Tool Evolution for Analytics over data Lakes) is a method that helps coding agents create reusable data-analysis tools without needing labeled data. It combines two types of agents: an Explorer that finds relevant data and a Critic that evaluates the effectiveness of the tools based on previous tasks. By evolving a library of tools, TEAL allows agents to improve their performance on analytical questions while minimizing redundant work. The approach shows that even without ground-truth labels, effective tools can be developed through unsupervised learning and iterative feedback.

zh.title: 无标签环境下的工具进化与数据分析
zh.desc: TEAL（数据湖分析工具进化）是一种为编码代理开发可重用数据分析工具的方法，旨在在没有真实标签的情况下，通过数据驱动的探索和基于轨迹的批评来提高准确性。该方法允许代理在处理数据湖时发现、清理和连接相关数据，而不是每次都从头开始。TEAL通过自动构建和优化工具库，帮助代理在重复任务中提高效率。实验结果表明，TEAL在有限的步骤预算下显著提升了代理的表现，展示了在无监督环境中进化有用工具的潜力。

papers.title: HarnessRL: Co-Evolving Policies with a Just-in-Time Training Harness for Open-Ended RL
papers.abstract: Abstract HarnessRL co-evolves a training harness with the policy via adaptive task sampling, rollout guidance, and rubric updates to prevent reward failure in open-ended reinforcement learning.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Rubric-based reinforcement learning (RL) trains policies for open-ended generation with natural-language criteria as rewards, but these rewards can become ineffective as training progresses. We identify two failure modes. Under non-discriminative rewards, scores collapse to uniformly low or high values due to insufficient exploration or a mismatch between task difficulty and policy capability. Under spurious rewards, higher scores do not correspond to better responses. Both reflect a training configuration whose task sampling, exploration, and evaluation stay fixed as the policy evolves. We introduce HarnessRL, a training-time harness that co-evolves with the policy through three interfaces for task sampling, rollout guidance, and rubric criteria. HarnessRL maintains a training-time memory from which a harness evolver retrieves within-task history and cross-task evidence. Using this evidence, the evolver attributes each reward failure to the interface whose update can address it. It then runs a proposer and just-in-time critic loop in which the critic accepts a candidate update only after measuring its effect on the current frozen policy, returning rejected candidates for revision. We also curate Rubric-Mix-10k, a five-domain training and evaluation suite for open-ended RL across medical, science, writing, role-play, and instruction-following tasks. On Rubric-Mix-10k, HarnessRL outperforms the strongest baselines by 2.8 to 3.1 points across both 4B and 9B model scales and nearly halves the training steps to its best checkpoint. Code and data are available at https://github.com/Tongyi-ConvAI/Qwen-Character/tree/main/HarnessRL.

ru.title: Обучающая обвязка, которая растёт вместе с моделью, спасает reward от поломок
ru.desc: В статье представлен HarnessRL — обучающий фреймворк, который совместно эволюционирует вместе с policy модели и управляет выборкой задач, guidance для rollout и критериями rubric в reinforcement learning. Авторы выделяют два типа сбоев наград: non-discriminative rewards, когда оценки схлопываются, и spurious rewards, когда высокий балл не соответствует качеству ответа. Для их устранения используется память обучения, harness evolver и цикл proposer и just-in-time critic, который принимает обновления только после проверки их эффекта на замороженной модели. На новом наборе Rubric-Mix-10k метод превосходит сильнейшие baseline на 2.8–3.1 пункта для моделей 4B и 9B и почти вдвое сокращает число шагов обучения.

en.title: HarnessRL: Evolving Training for Effective Reinforcement Learning
en.desc: HarnessRL is a novel approach in reinforcement learning that adapts the training process alongside the evolving policy to enhance performance in open-ended tasks. It addresses common issues like non-discriminative and spurious rewards that can hinder effective learning by dynamically adjusting task sampling, rollout guidance, and evaluation criteria. By maintaining a memory of past interactions, HarnessRL can identify and rectify reward failures, ensuring that the training remains relevant and effective. The method has shown significant improvements in performance on the Rubric-Mix-10k benchmark, demonstrating its efficiency in reducing training time while achieving better results.

zh.title: HarnessRL：优化开放式强化学习的训练框架
zh.desc: HarnessRL是一种训练框架，它通过自适应任务采样、回滚指导和评分标准更新，与策略共同进化，以防止开放式强化学习中的奖励失败。我们发现了两种失败模式：一种是非区分性奖励，导致得分均匀低或高，另一种是虚假奖励，高得分并不代表更好的响应。HarnessRL通过三个接口来共同进化策略，维护训练时的记忆，以便在策略演变过程中调整任务采样和评估。实验结果表明，HarnessRL在Rubric-Mix-10k数据集上显著优于其他基线，训练步骤几乎减少了一半。

papers.title: Harness Self-Evolution for Long-Horizon Terminal Agents
papers.abstract: Abstract RiseHarness iteratively improves agent harness reliability by analyzing execution traces and integrating mechanisms from other frameworks without altering model weights.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Long-horizon terminal agents may solve a task in one run yet fail across repeated runs. Stochastic errors can propagate through actions and context, creating a gap between capability and reliable execution. We present RiseHarness, a framework for iteratively improving agent harnesses with model weights fixed. It focuses on flipping tasks with both successful and failed runs under the same configuration, using successful runs as references for failure analysis. RiseHarness combines agent trajectories with internal harness traces from a runtime monitor to examine how model actions interact with command execution, feedback, context management, and completion decisions. A Harness Handbook links this evidence to harness behaviors and source code, helping identify recurring problems in mechanisms shared across tasks. RiseHarness then searches other harness frameworks for relevant implementations and adapts them as design references to the current model and execution protocol. Candidate changes undergo behavioral checks and repeated task evaluation; versions with measured gains seed the next iteration. This loop integrates suitable mechanisms from different frameworks into a single harness and uses new execution evidence to guide further changes. We evaluate task success and reliability across models, ablate harness execution evidence and external research, and test transfer to unseen benchmarks with the same model. RiseHarness treats a specific model as the unit of harness adaptation, studying how changes to shared interaction mechanisms can make existing capabilities more reliable across tasks.

ru.title: Надёжность агента растёт не из весов модели, а из её обвязки
ru.desc: Статья представляет RiseHarness — фреймворк, который итеративно улучшает обвязку (harness) LLM-агента без изменения весов модели. Система анализирует траектории выполнения и внутренние трейсы рантайм-монитора, находя повторяющиеся сбои в одних и тех же конфигурациях. Затем она заимствует подходящие механизмы из других фреймворков, проверяет изменения и отбирает версии с реальным приростом качества. Подход повышает надёжность агентов в длинных задачах на терминале и переносится на новые бенчмарки с той же моделью.

en.title: Enhancing Agent Reliability Through Iterative Harness Improvement
en.desc: RiseHarness is a framework designed to enhance the reliability of agent harnesses without changing the model weights. It analyzes execution traces from both successful and failed task runs to identify and address recurring issues in agent behavior. By integrating mechanisms from other frameworks, RiseHarness iteratively adapts these solutions to improve performance while maintaining a fixed model. This approach allows for a systematic evaluation of task success and reliability, ultimately leading to more dependable agent execution across various tasks.

zh.title: 逐步提升智能体可靠性的框架
zh.desc: RiseHarness 是一个框架，旨在通过分析执行轨迹来逐步提高智能体的可靠性，而不改变模型的权重。它关注在相同配置下成功和失败的运行，通过成功的运行作为失败分析的参考。该框架结合了智能体的轨迹和运行时监控的内部数据，研究模型动作如何与命令执行、反馈、上下文管理和完成决策相互作用。RiseHarness 还从其他框架中寻找相关实现，并将其适应当前模型和执行协议，以提高任务的成功率和可靠性。

papers.title: Large Flow Language Models
papers.abstract: Abstract A large-scale continuous flow language model achieves efficient training, high-quality generation, and faster inference through blockwise flow design, self-speculative decoding, and multi-token prediction.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Continuous flow language models offer a path to parallel generation with tools for control and acceleration unavailable to discrete diffusion, yet effective techniques for building them at the billion-parameter scale remain less established. We present Lafa (Large flow language model), a fast, high-performing flow language model scaled to 8B parameters in a data-efficient manner. Lafa is a blockwise flow model with causal attention on the prefix and bidirectional, asynchronous flow within each block. This design enables efficient training by adapting pretrained autoregressive (AR) models and fast inference via prefix caching and blockwise parallel decoding. We train Lafa at 0.5B, 7B, and 8B scales with fewer than 30B tokens, more efficient than previous diffusion models, and evaluate it on instruction following, reasoning, and coding, where the learned flow matches or surpasses the quality of AR and can be distilled into flow maps for one- and few-step generation. Notably, flow training preserves or even improves pretrained AR capabilities via a multi-token prediction effect, which we leverage in a self-speculative decoding scheme that verifies flow-based drafts autoregressively within a single model. This yields 2.54x the throughput of an AR model at comparable quality, outperforming multi-token prediction and discrete diffusion methods. Our findings show that continuous flows can serve as a scalable foundation for language modeling.

ru.title: Непрерывный поток вместо пошагового вывода: параллельная генерация текста в 2.5 раза быстрее
ru.desc: В статье представлена Lafa — языковая модель на основе непрерывных потоков (flow language model) с 8 миллиардами параметров, которая обучается эффективно за счёт блочного дизайна и адаптации предобученных AR-моделей. Модель использует причинное внимание на префиксе и двунаправленный асинхронный flow внутри каждого блока, что позволяет быстро генерировать текст с помощью кэширования префикса и блочного параллельного декодирования. Авторы показывают, что качество Lafa на задачах следования инструкциям, рассуждений и программирования не уступает AR-моделям, а дистилляция в flow maps даёт генерацию за один-несколько шагов. Метод self-speculative decoding, основанный на эффекте multi-token prediction, даёт прирост пропускной способности в 2.54 раза по сравнению с AR-моделью при сопоставимом качестве.

en.title: Lafa: Revolutionizing Language Models with Continuous Flow
en.desc: This paper introduces Lafa, a large-scale continuous flow language model designed for efficient training and fast inference. It utilizes a blockwise flow architecture with causal attention and asynchronous flow, allowing it to adapt pretrained autoregressive models effectively. Lafa achieves high performance with 8 billion parameters while requiring fewer training tokens compared to previous models. The innovative self-speculative decoding method enhances throughput significantly, demonstrating that continuous flow models can be a powerful alternative for language generation tasks.

zh.title: 连续流模型：语言建模的新基础
zh.desc: 这篇论文介绍了一种名为Lafa的大规模连续流语言模型，具有高效的训练和快速的推理能力。Lafa采用了块状流设计和自我推测解码，能够在生成过程中实现并行处理。通过对预训练自回归模型的适应，Lafa在数据效率上表现优异，并在指令跟随、推理和编码任务中超越了传统的自回归模型。研究结果表明，连续流模型可以作为语言建模的可扩展基础。

papers.title: EAU: Environment-Agent-User Co-evolution for Training User-Centric Agents
papers.abstract: Abstract EAU is a meta-agent framework that co-evolves the user simulator, environment, and reinforcement learning setup alongside the policy to improve multi-turn LLM agent training.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Training LLM agents to interact with users over multiple turns is challenging because the learning signal depends not only on the agent, but also on the user simulator and environment, which jointly shape the agent's experience. Simulated users can be stochastic or inconsistent, while environments may contain unreliable tools, incomplete state coverage, and incorrect verifiers. Prior work mainly addresses the resulting instability through reward shaping or denser supervision, while treating these components as fixed. We instead introduce EAU, a meta-agent framework for environment--agent--user co-evolution. During training, EAU monitors trajectories, tool traces, rewards, and training statistics; diagnoses failures and uninformative interactions; and proposes targeted modifications to the user simulator, environment, reward design, and RL configuration. Validated changes are hot-swapped into the ongoing run, allowing the training setup to evolve together with the policy. These adaptations also persist across runs, so later training can build on previously discovered improvements rather than restarting from a fixed setup. We enable this process through an editable symbolic representation of user and environment dynamics, while the agent remains a neural LLM optimized with RL. Across three interactive-agent benchmarks and two backbone models, EAU consistently outperforms prior RL methods, improving the overall score over the strongest baseline by 14.7--15.0% and increasing successful task completion on ColBench by up to 36.7%, showing that co-evolving the training system with the policy can substantially improve multi-turn RL.

ru.title: Обучай агента и среду вместе: совместная эволюция системы обучения сильнее фиксированной настройки
ru.desc: В статье представлен EAU — meta-agent фреймворк, который совместно эволюционирует симулятор пользователя, среду и настройки reinforcement learning вместе с policy LLM-агента. Во время обучения система анализирует траектории, трассировки инструментов и награды, выявляет ошибки и неинформативные взаимодействия и предлагает целевые правки, которые применяются на лету без перезапуска. Среда и симулятор описываются редактируемым символьным представлением, а сам агент остаётся нейросетевой LLM, оптимизируемой через RL. На трёх интерактивных бенчмарках и двух backbone-моделях EAU стабильно превосходит предыдущие RL-методы, улучшая общий результат на 14.7–15.0% и повышая успешность выполнения задач на ColBench до 36.7%.

en.title: Co-evolving Training for Better Multi-turn LLM Agents
en.desc: The paper introduces EAU, a meta-agent framework designed to enhance the training of multi-turn language model (LLM) agents by co-evolving the user simulator, environment, and reinforcement learning (RL) setup alongside the agent's policy. This approach addresses the challenges posed by stochastic user behaviors and unreliable environments, which can lead to instability in training. EAU actively monitors various training metrics and dynamically adjusts the user simulator and environment based on identified failures, allowing for real-time improvements during the training process. The results demonstrate that EAU significantly outperforms traditional RL methods, leading to better task completion rates and overall performance in interactive-agent benchmarks.

zh.title: 共同进化，提升多轮强化学习的效果
zh.desc: EAU是一种元代理框架，它通过与策略共同进化用户模拟器、环境和强化学习设置，来改善多轮大语言模型（LLM）代理的训练。训练多轮交互的LLM代理具有挑战性，因为学习信号不仅依赖于代理本身，还依赖于用户模拟器和环境，这些因素共同塑造了代理的体验。EAU通过监控轨迹、工具痕迹、奖励和训练统计数据，诊断失败和无信息交互，并提出针对性的修改建议，从而实现环境、代理和用户的共同进化。经过验证的修改可以在运行过程中热插拔，使训练设置与策略一起演变，从而显著提高多轮强化学习的效果。

papers.title: Evaluating Agentic Capabilities Before Post-Training: An End-to-End Approach
papers.abstract: Abstract ASAP is a lightweight framework that evaluates agentic behavior in pretrained base models via interactive end-to-end tasks without converting them to chat agents.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Agentic capabilities are increasingly important for modern LLMs, yet remain difficult to evaluate during pretraining. Existing approaches typically rely on static trajectory-derived tasks or likelihood-based proxies, which are lightweight but provide limited visibility into how base models behave in interactive environments. We introduce ASAP (Agent Scaffold Adaptation for Pretraining Evaluation), a lightweight framework for eliciting and evaluating agentic behavior from pretrained base models on end-to-end tasks. Rather than converting base models into chat-style agents, ASAP preserves the completion interface and adapts existing agent scaffolds through structured trajectory continuation, short reference prefixes, and minimal recovery mechanisms. Across software-engineering and deep-research benchmarks, ASAP yields discriminative end-to-end performance across base models and pretraining checkpoints. Beyond aggregate scores, ASAP exposes model-generated execution trajectories, enabling analysis of exploration, editing, testing, recovery, and task completion across training stages. These trajectories provide a behavioral view of how agent-relevant capabilities change during pretraining and how execution patterns differ after post-training. Our results suggest that end-to-end agent evaluation can complement conventional pretraining benchmarks by providing a practical diagnostic of interactive model behavior.

ru.title: Оцениваем агентность базовых LLM без превращения их в чат-ботов
ru.desc: Статья представляет ASAP — лёгкий фреймворк для оценки агентного поведения предобученных базовых LLM в интерактивных задачах без их преобразования в чат-агентов. Вместо chat-формата сохраняется интерфейс дополнения текста, а существующие agent scaffolds адаптируются через structured trajectory continuation, короткие reference prefixes и минимальные механизмы восстановления. На бенчмарках software engineering и deep research ASAP даёт различимые end-to-end метрики для разных моделей и чекпоинтов предобучения. Модуль также анализирует сгенерированные траектории выполнения (исследование, редактирование, тестирование, восстановление), показывая, как агентные навыки меняются в ходе обучения, и дополняя традиционные pretraining-бенчмарки.

en.title: Evaluating Agentic Behavior in Pretrained Models with ASAP
en.desc: ASAP is a new framework designed to assess the agentic behavior of pretrained language models without turning them into chat agents. It focuses on evaluating how these models perform in interactive tasks by using structured methods that maintain their original completion interface. The framework allows for detailed analysis of model behavior through execution trajectories, revealing insights into their capabilities during pretraining. By providing a more dynamic evaluation approach, ASAP enhances our understanding of model performance beyond traditional benchmarks.

zh.title: ASAP：评估预训练模型的代理行为新方法
zh.desc: ASAP是一个轻量级框架，用于通过交互式端到端任务评估预训练基础模型的代理行为，而无需将其转换为聊天代理。现有的方法通常依赖于静态轨迹任务或基于似然的代理，这些方法虽然轻量，但对基础模型在交互环境中的行为提供的可见性有限。ASAP通过结构化轨迹延续、简短参考前缀和最小恢复机制，适应现有的代理框架，从而保留了完成接口。我们的研究表明，ASAP能够在软件工程和深度研究基准测试中，提供基础模型和预训练检查点的区分性端到端性能。

papers.title: On the Fragility of Tasks under Composition: Implicit Budgeting in Language Models
papers.abstract: Abstract  Modern language models are increasingly asked to handle several tasks within a single prompt. Doing so requires solving each task correctly while integrating the resulting answers into a coherent response. In this paper, we identify a fundamental limitation in this process, where models make substantially more errors when tasks are composed, even when they can solve every constituent task reliably in isolation. This degradation cannot be fully explained by the accumulation of independent errors. Across both open-weight models and the frontier model Claude Opus 5, our findings instead point to an implicit thinking budget underlying this effect. In particular, under composition, models use substantially fewer tokens per task than in isolation, even when the full sequence remains well within the context window. Tasks that require longer solution traces in isolation are consequently more fragile under composition, i.e., models make more errors on prompts containing these tasks. In isolation, non-fragile tasks receive more reasoning than they need and waste compute. However, by grouping tasks according to their fragility, the implicit budgeting can be manipulated to reduce token usage by 43\% across a range of math and linguistic tasks while also preserving accuracy.

ru.title: Модель экономит токены там, где они нужнее всего
ru.desc: В статье исследуется, почему LLM хуже справляются с несколькими задачами, объединёнными в один промпт, даже если каждую из них по отдельности модель решает надёжно. Авторы показывают, что деградация не объясняется простым накоплением независимых ошибок, а связана с неявным thinking budget: при композиции модели тратят заметно меньше токенов на каждую задачу. Задачи, требующие длинных цепочек рассуждений, оказываются наиболее хрупкими в такой постановке, а простые задачи получают избыточный compute. Группировка задач по их хрупкости позволяет управлять этим бюджетом и сократить расход токенов на 43% без потери точности.

en.title: Optimizing Task Composition in Language Models
en.desc: This paper explores how modern language models struggle when asked to perform multiple tasks at once, even if they can handle each task well on its own. The authors found that when tasks are combined, models tend to use fewer tokens, leading to more mistakes, especially for tasks that require more complex reasoning. This issue arises from an implicit 'thinking budget' that limits how much processing the model allocates to each task when they are composed together. By organizing tasks based on their complexity, the researchers demonstrate that it's possible to reduce token usage significantly while maintaining accuracy in the model's responses.

zh.title: 优化任务组合，提升模型表现
zh.desc: 现代语言模型在处理多个任务时面临挑战，尤其是在同一提示中完成多个任务时。研究发现，当任务组合在一起时，模型的错误率显著增加，即使它们在单独处理每个任务时表现良好。这种性能下降并不能仅仅通过独立错误的累积来解释，而是与模型在处理组合任务时的隐性思维预算有关。通过根据任务的脆弱性对任务进行分组，可以有效减少计算资源的使用，同时保持准确性。

papers.title: More Memory, Worse Agents: Error Reproduction and Anti-Persistence in LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Abstract Anti-Persistence improves LLM agent self-improvement by accumulating execution experience while discarding synthesized guidance after use, reducing error reproduction and cost.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small LLM agents can improve across tasks without updating model parameters by storing experience from their own executions in external memory and reusing it to guide later decisions. A central design question is whether to retain only observed trajectories and outcomes or also the rules, summaries, and skills inferred from them. Retaining these abstractions allows agents to reuse strategies without repeatedly deriving them from raw trajectories. However, errors in stored abstractions can propagate to subsequent decisions through retrieval and reuse. They can also shape execution trajectories, which then become the basis for new abstractions that reproduce the original errors. We term this feedback mechanism error reproduction: errors are regenerated through a cycle of abstraction, execution, and re-abstraction, extending their persistence beyond direct reuse of the original faulty knowledge. We propose Anti-Persistence, a memory design that accumulates trajectories and outcomes while reconstructing task-specific guidance on demand. An adaptive selector uses prior outcomes to decide whether and how to synthesize guidance, which is discarded after execution. This prevents its direct reuse as a stored object, although indirect feedback through retained trajectories remains possible. Across different benchmarks and backbones, Anti-Persistence achieves higher overall held-out success and the lowest average LLM-call cost among the evaluated memory designs. These results support separating experience accumulation from abstraction persistence in memorybased self-improvement.

ru.title: Копи опыт, но не храни готовые выводы: память без закрепления ошибок
ru.desc: В статье рассматривается самосовершенствование LLM-агентов через внешнюю память, где накапливается опыт их собственных выполнений без обновления параметров модели. Авторы показывают, что сохранение выведенных абстракций (правил и навыков) может приводить к феномену «воспроизведения ошибок»: ошибочные обобщения распространяются через цикл абстракции, выполнения и повторной абстракции. Предлагается метод Anti-Persistence, который сохраняет только траектории и результаты, а руководство синтезирует на лету адаптивным селектором и отбрасывает после использования. Эксперименты на разных бенчмарках и backbone-моделях показывают более высокую успешность на held-out данных и наименьшую среднюю стоимость вызовов LLM среди сравниваемых методов памяти.

en.title: Enhancing LLM Self-Improvement with Anti-Persistence
en.desc: This paper introduces Anti-Persistence, a method that enhances the self-improvement of LLM agents by managing how they store and use their execution experiences. Instead of keeping all synthesized guidance, Anti-Persistence focuses on retaining only the execution trajectories and outcomes, which helps reduce the risk of repeating errors. The approach allows agents to adaptively generate task-specific guidance when needed, while preventing the direct reuse of potentially faulty abstractions. The results show that this method leads to better performance and lower costs in various benchmarks, highlighting the importance of separating experience accumulation from the persistence of abstractions.

zh.title: 反持久性：提升LLM代理自我改进的创新设计
zh.desc: 反持久性通过积累执行经验并在使用后丢弃合成指导，改善了大型语言模型（LLM）代理的自我改进，降低了错误再现和成本。代理可以在不更新模型参数的情况下，通过外部记忆存储自己的执行经验，并在后续决策中重用这些经验。关键设计问题是保留观察到的轨迹和结果，还是也保留从中推断出的规则、摘要和技能。我们提出的反持久性是一种记忆设计，能够在需求时重建特定任务的指导，从而提高整体成功率并降低平均调用成本。

papers.title: HybridResearcher: Bridging the Structured-Unstructured Boundary for Deep Research Agents
papers.abstract: Abstract HybridResearcher is a small agent trained via synthetic cross-source trajectories and reinforcement learning to reason across structured and unstructured data, outperforming much larger models without forgetting single-source skills.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small While LLM agents are increasingly capable of gathering and synthesizing evidence from a single homogeneous source, such as structured tables or unstructured data, real-world analytical questions frequently span heterogeneous sources. For example, answering one enterprise question may require both a result computed over an internal database and evidence found on the web. Recent evaluations on benchmarks like HybridDeepResearch show that even frontier agents struggle when evidence must cross this boundary. While these benchmarks have exposed the limitation, methodologies to explicitly teach cross-source reasoning remain absent. To address this, we introduce HybridResearcher, a 4B agent trained to bridge evidence across the structured and unstructured boundary. To build it, we synthesize cross-source bridge trajectories by starting with validated single-source tasks-such as existing text-to-SQL or web search queries-and fabricating the missing source around a bridge entity drawn from the seed's own output. We retain a sample only when strict construction gates confirm that neither side alone suffices, ensuring the data requires true cross-source interdependence. Finally, we train on this curated dataset using supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning. Evaluated on the existing HybridDeepResearch benchmark, HybridResearcher improves over our base model, Qwen3.5-4B, by 30.0 points pass@8 and surpasses the far larger Qwen3.5-397B-A17B by 8.3 points, while also improving over its base model on established, held-out single-source benchmarks (BrowseComp and BrowseComp-Plus), demonstrating that this complex cross-source reasoning can be taught directly to small models without triggering catastrophic forgetting.
affiliations: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

ru.title: Маленькая модель учится связывать таблицы и веб без потери навыков
ru.desc: Авторы представляют HybridResearcher — небольшого LLM-агента на 4B параметров, который учится связывать данные из структурированных (таблицы, базы данных) и неструктурированных (веб) источников. Для обучения создаётся синтетический датасет кросс-источниковых траекторий: к проверенным однотипным задачам (например, text-to-SQL или веб-поиск) добавляется недостающий источник вокруг общей сущности, а строгие фильтры оставляют только примеры, где ни один источник не достаточен сам по себе. Модель дообучается сначала через supervised fine-tuning, а затем через reinforcement learning. В результате HybridResearcher превосходит базовую модель Qwen3.5-4B на 30 пунктов pass@8 и даже более крупную Qwen3.5-397B-A17B на 8.3 пункта, сохраняя качество на однотипных бенчмарках без catastrophic forgetting.

en.title: Bridging Data Sources with HybridResearcher
en.desc: HybridResearcher is a compact AI agent designed to effectively reason across different types of data, both structured and unstructured, using reinforcement learning. It excels in tasks that require integrating information from various sources, outperforming larger models while retaining its ability to handle single-source tasks. The training process involves creating synthetic data that emphasizes the need for cross-source reasoning, ensuring that the model learns to connect disparate pieces of evidence. Evaluations show significant improvements in performance on benchmarks, indicating that smaller models can achieve advanced reasoning capabilities without losing their foundational skills.

zh.title: 跨源推理的新突破
zh.desc: HybridResearcher 是一个通过合成跨源轨迹和强化学习训练的小型智能体，能够在结构化和非结构化数据之间进行推理，且表现优于更大的模型。该模型解决了在真实世界分析问题中，常常需要跨越异构数据源的挑战。通过合成跨源桥接轨迹，HybridResearcher 能够有效地整合来自内部数据库和网络的证据。最终的评估结果显示，该模型在多个基准测试中均表现出色，证明了小型模型也能直接学习复杂的跨源推理而不会遗忘单一来源的技能。

papers.title: Beyond Compilation: Evaluating Faithful Natural-Language-to-Lean Statement Formalization
papers.abstract: Abstract The study evaluates whether Lean compilation alone ensures faithful statement autoformalization, finding substantial gaps between compiling and semantically accepted outputs across multiple systems, with tool-augmented agents improving compilation but still exhibiting real translation errors.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Lean verifies that a generated declaration is well typed, but cannot check whether it states what the user intended. We measure how far compilation overstates faithfulness in statement autoformalization without canonical Lean targets. Our criterion requires Lean compilation and agreement of two LLM judges from different model families. On an independent random audit, it agrees with the human majority on 91.5% of cases; it rarely accepts an unfaithful output but rejects some faithful ones. Across eight systems on 227 university-level statements, the gap between compiling and accepted outputs ranges from 1.3 to 29.5 percentage points: our tool-augmented agent compiles 87.2% of the statements, but only 57.7% are accepted. Human review of all the agent's rejections confirms that 23.8 of its 29.5 points are real translation errors. For the gaps of the seven one-shot systems, a two-stage review by Claude Opus 5.5 with Lean and GPT-6.1 Sol, validated on these human labels, finds that 78-100% are real translation errors for six of them. When GPT-5.2, one of the two judges, grades the translations of two models released after it, GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5, it accepts 83% of the statements for each, against 21% for one-shot GPT-5.2. For these two models, the same review classifies only 4 of their 54 rejections (7%) as translation errors, so most of their measured gap is judge errors rather than translation errors. This is consistent with these systems erring less while the judge does not: the fewer errors a system makes, the smaller the share of its rejections that are translation errors. Finally, a 2^3 tool ablation of the agent shows that Lean feedback drives most of its compilation gain, and that nearly half of this gain fails the semantic criterion. Code and data are available at https://github.com/grenadeComing/beyond-compilation.

ru.title: Компиляция не равна смыслу: проверка Lean не гарантирует верность перевода
ru.desc: Статья показывает, что компиляция в Lean не гарантирует семантическую точность автоформализации математических утверждений: разрыв между скомпилированными и принятыми переводами достигает 29,5 процентных пунктов. Авторы предлагают критерий, сочетающий компиляцию с согласием двух LLM-судей из разных семейств моделей, который совпадает с мнением людей в 91,5% случаев. Ручной анализ показывает, что большинство отклонений агента являются реальными ошибками перевода, однако у самых сильных моделей значительная часть разрыва вызвана ошибками судьи, а не перевода. Абляция инструментов агента выявляет, что обратная связь от Lean даёт основную часть прироста компиляции, но почти половина этого прироста не проходит семантический критерий.

en.title: Bridging the Gap: Lean Compilation vs. Semantic Accuracy
en.desc: This paper investigates the effectiveness of Lean compilation in ensuring that automatically generated statements are semantically accurate. It reveals significant discrepancies between the outputs produced by Lean compilation and those accepted by human judges, indicating that compilation alone does not guarantee faithful autoformalization. The study employs a two-stage review process involving large language models (LLMs) to assess the accuracy of the generated statements, finding that many rejections stem from judge errors rather than translation errors. Ultimately, the research highlights the importance of tool-augmented agents in improving compilation accuracy, while also emphasizing the limitations of relying solely on compilation for semantic correctness.

zh.title: Lean编译的真实翻译挑战
zh.desc: 本研究评估了仅依靠Lean编译是否能确保声明的自动形式化是准确的。研究发现，编译输出与语义接受输出之间存在显著差距，尽管工具增强的代理改善了编译，但仍然出现真实的翻译错误。通过对227个大学级声明的分析，发现编译的声明中只有57.7%被接受，且大部分拒绝的声明确实存在翻译错误。最终，研究表明Lean反馈是提升编译效果的主要驱动力，但近一半的提升未能满足语义标准。

papers.title: WinARDet: Compressed Window Auto-Regression for Long-Horizon Vision-Language Grounding
papers.abstract: Abstract Compressed Window Auto-Regression partitions long answer sequences into windows with restricted autoregression and compressed latent history to prevent attention takeover and box repetition in dense vision-language grounding.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small MLLM-based detectors formulate vision-language grounding as autoregressive coordinate generation, yet in dense scenes, they often collapse into a box repetition loop, repeatedly emitting identical boxes until the decoding budget is exhausted. We trace this failure to historical-answer attention takeover: Under full-history autoregression, repeated coordinate tokens in the growing answer history attract disproportionate attention, crowding out the attention sinks needed to attend to new visual evidence. % To break this loop, in this paper, we propose Compressed Window Auto-Regression (WinAR). This new mechanism partitions a long answer sequence into consecutive generation windows and restricts full token-level autoregression to the current window only while compressing each previous window into a fixed set of latent tokens that condition subsequent decoding. This design reduces the repeated exposure to raw historical coordinates that triggers the attention takeover, yet preserves cross-window dependencies essential for coherent multi-object generation. On RSDense, which contains 200-2,000 objects per image, our model WinARDet improves RexOmni F1-score (IoU=0.5) from 32.16 to 39.36 over the baseline, while reducing the redundancy rate from 35.48% to 13.00%. WinARDet also generalizes across decoding strategies and output formats, including parallel box decoding and polygon generation, providing a practical paradigm for long-horizon vision-language grounding across scene densities.

ru.title: Окна вместо бесконечного повторения: сжимаем историю, чтобы видеть новые объекты
ru.desc: Авторы рассматривают задачу vision-language grounding в плотных сценах, где MLLM-детекторы генерируют координаты объектов авторегрессионно и часто зацикливаются, повторяя одинаковые боксы. Причина проблемы в том, что при полной авторегрессии по всей истории ответа повторяющиеся токены координат перетягивают на себя attention и вытесняют attention sinks, необходимые для поиска новых визуальных признаков. Предложенный механизм Compressed Window Auto-Regression (WinAR) делит длинную последовательность ответа на окна, внутри текущего окна применяет полную авторегрессию, а предыдущие окна сжимает в фиксированный набор латентных токенов. На датасете RSDense метод WinARDet повышает F1-score (IoU=0.5) с 32.16 до 39.36 и снижает долю избыточных боксов с 35.48% до 13.00%, при этом подход работает и с параллельным декодированием, и с полигонами.

en.title: Breaking the Box Repetition Loop in Vision-Language Grounding
en.desc: This paper introduces Compressed Window Auto-Regression (WinAR), a method designed to improve vision-language grounding in dense scenes. The approach addresses the problem of attention takeover, where repeated coordinate tokens in the answer history dominate the model's focus, leading to box repetition. By partitioning long answer sequences into smaller windows and compressing previous windows into latent tokens, WinAR allows the model to generate responses without being overwhelmed by historical data. The results show significant improvements in performance metrics while reducing redundancy, making it effective for complex visual tasks.

zh.title: 压缩窗口自回归：解决视觉语言基础中的重复问题
zh.desc: 本文提出了一种新的机制，称为压缩窗口自回归（WinAR），用于解决视觉语言基础中的重复框问题。通过将长答案序列划分为连续的生成窗口，并限制全历史自回归仅在当前窗口内进行，WinAR有效地减少了对历史坐标的重复暴露。该方法在RSDense数据集上显著提高了模型的F1分数，并降低了冗余率，展示了其在密集场景中的有效性。WinARDet还能够适应不同的解码策略和输出格式，为长时间视觉语言基础提供了实用的范式。

papers.title: PhysLDM: Latent Diffusion for High-Fidelity Deformable Simulation
papers.abstract: Abstract PhysLDM introduces a spatiotemporal latent diffusion framework for high-fidelity deformable body simulation, using a holistic VAE and diffusion to model chaotic dynamics and enable zero-shot generalization.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Neural simulation of high-fidelity deformable bodies is a foundational challenge in computer graphics and physical AI. Long-horizon prediction for high-resolution 3D volumetric meshes is hard: autoregressive methods are prone to error accumulation, while direct multi-frame prediction at native resolution is computationally prohibitive. This motivates a compact spatiotemporal latent representation, which is largely unexplored for mesh-based volumetric physics. Meanwhile, it remains unclear whether deterministic regression or generative diffusion is the more suitable predictive paradigm. To address these coupled challenges, we introduce PhysLDM, a unified latent-diffusion paradigm for one-shot deformable simulation. Its core is a holistic spatiotemporal VAE that avoids the "staircase" artifacts of standard temporal compression (e.g., video VAEs), achieving ~2.48 mm reconstruction precision on meter-scale scenes at up to 78x token compression. Based on this reliable latent space, we systematically compare regression and diffusion methods. Our experiments uncover a key modeling insight: complex deformable dynamics are often chaotic, and in this regime deterministic regression tends to produce non-physical averages, whereas diffusion better models their distribution. Accordingly, we employ a latent diffusion model that effectively learns from chaotic data to generate physically plausible trajectories. Trained purely kinematically on an Objaverse-scale dataset, a single PhysLDM generalizes zero-shot to unseen OOD datasets. Its differentiability further enables efficient solution of inverse problems and higher-order design optimization. To our knowledge, PhysLDM is the first high-fidelity spatiotemporal autoencoder and latent-diffusion paradigm for volumetric deformable dynamics, offering a scalable and robust approach to neural simulation. Project Page: https://yucrazing.github.io/physldm/
affiliations: Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory, Shanghai, China

ru.title: Диффузия в латентном пространстве побеждает регрессию в моделировании хаотичных деформаций
ru.desc: Статья представляет PhysLDM — латентную диффузионную модель для нейросетевого моделирования деформируемых 3D-тел с помощью единого пространственно-временного VAE, который сжимает объёмные меши без артефактов «ступенек» и достигает точности около 2.48 мм при сжатии до 78 раз. Авторы показывают, что динамика деформаций часто хаотична, и в таком режиме детерминированная регрессия даёт нефизичные усреднённые результаты, тогда как диффузия лучше моделирует распределение траекторий. Модель обучается чисто кинематически на датасете масштаба Objaverse и демонстрирует zero-shot generalization на неизвестных OOD-данных. Дифференцируемость модели позволяет эффективно решать обратные задачи и оптимизировать проектирование.

en.title: Revolutionizing Deformable Body Simulation with Latent Diffusion
en.desc: PhysLDM is a new framework that uses a spatiotemporal latent diffusion model to simulate deformable bodies in a realistic way. It combines a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) with diffusion techniques to handle the chaotic nature of these dynamics, allowing for accurate predictions without needing extensive computational resources. The model achieves high precision in reconstructing 3D volumetric meshes while effectively generalizing to new datasets without prior training. This approach not only improves the simulation of complex movements but also facilitates solving inverse problems and optimizing designs efficiently.

zh.title: 高保真可变形体模拟的新方法
zh.desc: PhysLDM提出了一种时空潜在扩散框架，用于高保真可变形体的模拟。该方法结合了整体变分自编码器（VAE）和扩散模型，能够有效处理混沌动态并实现零样本泛化。通过构建紧凑的时空潜在表示，PhysLDM克服了传统自回归方法的误差累积问题，并在高分辨率3D体积网格预测中表现出色。实验结果表明，扩散模型在处理复杂的可变形动态时，能够更好地捕捉其分布特征，生成物理上合理的轨迹。

papers.title: PVBench: Quantifying Physical Plausibility in Video Generation with Object-Level Physical Measurements
papers.abstract: Abstract PVBench introduces a quantitative benchmark with 46 physical dimensions to evaluate the plausibility of generated videos using specialized vision models and human-aligned metrics.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Recent video generation models produce visually compelling outputs, yet their physical plausibility remains poorly measured. Physical plausibility asks whether generated objects obey geometry, kinematics, dynamics, and conservation laws. Existing benchmarks rely on coarse visual-language model judgments or target embodied world models rather than video generation itself. We introduce PVBench, a physical video benchmark that quantitatively measures the plausibility of generated videos across 46 dimensions organized into seven domains, spanning: i) instruction and semantic fidelity, ii) behavioral and causal consistency, iii) perceptual and temporal quality, iv) geometric and spatial consistency, v) material properties and field states, vi) kinematic and spatiotemporal persistence, vii) and mechanical plausibility with conservation laws. PVBench comprises 600 carefully crafted prompts, of which 30% involve physical embodied agents such as robot arms, humanoids, quadrupeds, and multi-agent systems. For challenging physically tractable dimensions, it pairs each with specialized vision models that derive verifiable, physically grounded measurements, such as object-level 6D pose, metric scale, surface normals, kinematics, and numerical conservation-law residuals. It thus avoids relying solely on subjective scoring, while supporting both text-to-video and image-to-video generation. Finally, we validate the agreement between automatic metrics and human judgments through human evaluation. Meanwhile, we evaluate mainstream open-source and closed-source models and present several insights. By releasing the benchmark, prompts, and calibration protocol, we aim to foster physically grounded video generation.
affiliations: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

ru.title: Видео должно подчиняться законам физики: измеряем правдоподобие количественно
ru.desc: В статье представлен PVBench — количественный бенчмарк для оценки физической правдоподобности видео, сгенерированных моделями. Он включает 46 измеряемых параметров, сгруппированных в семь доменов: от семантической точности и причинно-следственной связи до геометрии, материалов и законов сохранения. Бенчмарк содержит 600 промптов, 30% из которых связаны с физическими агентами вроде роботов и гуманоидов, а для проверки используются специализированные vision-модели, измеряющие 6D-позы, масштаб и остаточные значения законов сохранения. Согласованность автоматических метрик с оценками людей подтверждена human evaluation, а сам бенчмарк, промпты и протокол калибровки опубликованы для развития физически обоснованной генерации видео.

en.title: Measuring the Reality of Generated Videos with PVBench
en.desc: PVBench is a new benchmark designed to assess the physical plausibility of generated videos using advanced vision models and metrics aligned with human perception. It evaluates videos across 46 specific dimensions that cover various aspects such as geometric accuracy, causal consistency, and material properties. By utilizing specialized vision models, PVBench provides objective measurements rather than relying on subjective evaluations. This benchmark aims to enhance the quality of video generation by ensuring that outputs adhere to fundamental physical laws and principles.

zh.title: 推动物理合理性的视频生成评估
zh.desc: PVBench是一个量化基准，包含46个物理维度，用于评估生成视频的物理合理性。生成的视频虽然在视觉上引人注目，但其物理合理性往往缺乏有效的测量。该基准通过七个领域的维度，系统地评估视频的几何、动力学和守恒定律等方面的表现。PVBench还结合了专门的视觉模型，提供可验证的物理测量，旨在推动基于物理的生成视频技术的发展。

papers.title: Muse Glimmer 30B: An On-Device Agentic Model
papers.abstract: Abstract Muse Glimmer is a 30B-parameter open-source causal language model with a perception encoder that performs multi-step reasoning and tool use locally on consumer hardware via 4-bit quantization.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small We introduce Muse Glimmer, an open-source 30B parameter causal language model with perception encoder, purpose-built for autonomous agentic tasks on consumer hardware. Muse Glimmer integrates multi-step reasoning, reliable tool use and failure recovery into a single model that runs locally on consumer devices without requiring cloud infrastructure. The model accepts text and image inputs and produces text outputs, was trained on data from over a hundred languages, and is quantized to approximately 4-bit precision for efficient single-GPU inference. Muse Glimmer achieves state-of-the-art performance for its size class on agentic benchmarks, setting a new standard compared to the models of its size: Gemma4-31B and Qwen3.6-27B on tool use, multi-step planning, and agentic task completion. We release the model under the Apache 2.0 license to foster open-source development of capable, safe, local AI agents.

ru.title: Мощный AI-агент, который работает прямо на вашем компьютере
ru.desc: В статье представлена Muse Glimmer — открытая causal language model (LLM) с 30 миллиардами параметров и perception encoder, которая обрабатывает текст и изображения. Модель обучена на данных более чем сотни языков и квантована примерно до 4-битной точности, что позволяет запускать её на одной потребительской GPU без облачной инфраструктуры. Авторы показывают, что Muse Glimmer достигает наилучших результатов среди моделей того же размера на agentic benchmarks, включая использование инструментов, многошаговое планирование и выполнение агентных задач. Модель выпущена под лицензией Apache 2.0, чтобы стимулировать открытую разработку локальных AI-агентов.

en.title: Empowering Local AI with Muse Glimmer
en.desc: Muse Glimmer is a powerful 30 billion parameter causal language model designed for autonomous tasks on consumer hardware. It features a perception encoder that allows it to process both text and image inputs while performing multi-step reasoning and tool use. The model is optimized for efficiency through 4-bit quantization, enabling it to run locally without relying on cloud services. Muse Glimmer sets a new benchmark in its category for agentic tasks, outperforming similar models in planning and tool utilization.

zh.title: Muse Glimmer：本地智能代理的新标准
zh.desc: Muse Glimmer是一种具有300亿参数的开源因果语言模型，专为在消费者硬件上执行自主任务而设计。它集成了多步推理、可靠的工具使用和故障恢复功能，能够在本地运行，无需依赖云基础设施。该模型支持文本和图像输入，并生成文本输出，经过训练的数据涵盖超过一百种语言，并进行了约4位精度的量化，以实现高效的单GPU推理。Muse Glimmer在代理基准测试中表现出色，设定了同类模型的新标准，推动了安全、高效的本地AI代理的发展。

papers.title: λ_0: Scaling Open-World Egocentric Human Data for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
papers.abstract: Abstract HumanVerse pairs egocentric video with synchronized body and hand motion to train a humanoid foundation model for whole-body loco-manipulation via human-to-robot transfer without target-task robot demonstrations.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Humanoid loco-manipulation requires coordinated whole-body interaction with the physical world, yet collecting robot demonstrations at scale remains costly. Human demonstrations offer a scalable alternative, but existing egocentric human supervision often omits locomotion and posture, while embodiment differences and controller dynamics hinder accurate end-effector execution. We introduce HumanVerse, a 500-hour dataset of open-world human loco-manipulation pairing egocentric video with synchronized body and hand motion. Our human-to-humanoid pipeline aligns camera viewpoints and arm appearance, and refines motion references and controller inputs offline to reduce end-effector errors while preserving whole-body coordination. We validate the pipeline through zero-shot transfer to Unitree G1 on representative whole-body manipulation and long-range loco-manipulation tasks, without target-task robot demonstrations. Building on this pipeline, we develop λ_0, a humanoid foundation model for whole-body loco-manipulation, with robot-aligned human demonstrations providing supervision for mid-training. Increasing whole-body human data consistently improves downstream task progress. λ_0 achieves 90.0% success on SIMPLE and 62.5% across real-world loco-manipulation tasks. We expect this study to guide scalable whole-body human data collection toward humanoid foundation models for richer interaction with the physical world. Homepage: https://lambdahumanoid.github.io/

ru.title: Учим гуманоидных роботов, наблюдая за людьми
